items.title: Oil's new problem isn't supply. It's logistics
items.author: Ron Bousso
items.creator: Ron Bousso
items.summary: Middle East crude exports recently climbed to their highest levels since the start of the Iran war as more Gulf producers resume transit through the Strait of Hormuz – despite the continued threat of Iranian attacks. Yet oil prices remain stubbornly elevated, suggesting logistical problems are proving as disruptive as outright supply losses.
items.body:
Middle East crude exports recently climbed to their highest levels since the start of the Iran war as more Gulf producers resume transit through the [USN:S8N43Z003 TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"] – despite the continued threat of Iranian attacks. Yet oil prices remain stubbornly elevated, suggesting logistical problems are proving as disruptive as outright supply losses.
Crude flows through the embattled waterway reached 14.2 million barrels per day on a seven-day average on Sept. 26, nearly 80% of pre-war levels, according to analytics firm Kpler. While volumes have declined since, they will likely be revised higher because ships often disable satellite tracking systems while traversing the strait and for several days thereafter.
Either way, the trend is clear: a lot more crude is getting through the strait. So why is Brent still trading above $100 per barrel?
In a word, logistics.
For decades, the global oil industry functioned as a finely tuned system designed to move enormous volumes of crude and fuels over long distances at the lowest possible cost. The conflicts in the Middle East and Eastern Europe have fractured that model, as a combination of record-high tanker rates, soaring insurance costs and a severe shortage of refining capacity has created bottlenecks across the energy supply chain.
Those problems may take months, if not years, to unwind, leaving consumers facing persistently high energy bills – even if the crude supply squeeze continues to ease.
BREAKING THE BLOCKADE Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz following the onset of the war with the US and Israel on February 28 rapidly reshaped global oil flows. Gulf producers diverted supplies through alternative routes, buyers sought barrels from more distant regions and governments released unprecedented volumes of oil from strategic reserves.
One of the biggest changes was that Saudi Arabia – previously the world’s largest oil exporter – diverted its exports through its [USN:L4N45E0KG TEXT:"East-West pipeline"], which delivers crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. At one point this year, 4% of global oil supplies were via this route.
However, after the pipeline came under attack by Iranian-backed Iraqi militias [USN:L6N4590XN TEXT:"in early September"], Saudi Arabia was forced to redirect exports back to the Gulf via Hormuz, which it discovered, could be more easily transited than previously thought.
Saudi exports through Hormuz averaged 3 million bpd in September, the highest level during the conflict, according to Kpler.
While Saudi Arabia’s crude exports through Hormuz in September were still only around half of pre-war volumes, the Kingdom’s exports could quickly near pre-war levels as the East-West pipeline [USN:L4N45E0KG TEXT:"gradually returns"] to normal operations.
Ironically, then, the attack on the East-West pipeline, which was intended to cripple Riyadh, may have instead weakened Tehran's most powerful leverage – its purported control of the Strait – by demonstrating that large volumes can still transit Hormuz and other major export hubs despite continued attacks.
GREAT FREIGHT Yet the recovery remains fragile.
On the one hand, the increase in Gulf exports has helped reduce the global oil deficit. Energy Aspects estimates the market now faces a shortfall of around 1.6 million bpd, down from roughly 4 million bpd during the peak disruption in May.
Under normal circumstances, such an improvement in supply would exert significant downward pressure on prices. Instead, Brent remains above $100 a barrel, more than 40% above pre-war levels.
Prices certainly reflect a substantial risk premium linked to the possibility of renewed escalation, as Washington and Tehran have still failed to reach any form of understanding over the future of Hormuz.
But geopolitics is only part of the story.
Freight and insurance costs, once a relatively minor component of the delivered price of oil, have become major price drivers.
This is partly due to the current [USN:L6N45A0SP TEXT:"shuttle system"] operating around the Gulf. Multiple tankers are frequently required to transport crude though Hormuz to the Gulf of Oman, where cargoes are transferred to smaller vessels before heading to buyers in Asia. This ties up significant numbers of very large crude carriers (VLCCs), reducing vessel availability elsewhere.
At the same time, buyers are increasingly sourcing crude from the Atlantic Basin and shipping it to Asia over longer routes, further tightening tanker supply.
The result has been a surge in key tanker rates to record highs.
Rates to transport crude from the Middle East to Asia aboard a VLCC recently exceeded $1.2 million per day, up from roughly $30,000 a day in January, according to shipping broker Poten & Partners.
As a result, freight costs that once accounted for around 3% of the delivered price of a barrel now represent roughly 27%.
These costs are unlikely to normalise until trade flows return to something resembling their pre-war pattern. Indeed, a further recovery in exports through Hormuz may initially worsen the situation by increasing demand for the elaborate shuttle networks now required to move crude safely through the region.
REFINING CRUNCH The loss of refining capacity in the Middle East and Russia, where Ukrainian drone attacks have crippled dozens of plants, has compounded the problem, particularly for diesel.
Diesel prices have surged to record highs, becoming a [USN:L6N45E0T3 TEXT:"major political concern"] for U.S. President Donald Trump ahead of next month's midterm elections, as diesel powers much of modern industry, agriculture and manufacturing.
The Group of Seven's decision last week to [USN:B5N44301Y TEXT:"release diesel"] from strategic stocks will likely provide only temporary relief as it does nothing to restore lost refining capacity.
What’s more, refiners are increasingly competing for the medium-sour crude grades that generate higher diesel yields. Those barrels are concentrated in the Middle East and Russia, precisely the regions where supply disruptions remain most severe.
That dynamic is creating a feedback loop. Tight refining capacity boosts diesel prices, which increases demand for diesel-rich crude grades, which in turn supports crude prices.
The result is that oil prices are no longer primarily a function of supply, but of the industry's ability to transport and process crude – making it much more challenging to bring these prices down.
(The opinions expressed here are those of Ron Bousso , a columnist for Reuters.)

items.title: India may be best placed to fill a China-sized hole in fuel exports
items.author: Gavin Maguire
items.creator: Gavin Maguire
items.summary: China's decision to suspend fuel exports for October has raised fresh fears of a further tightening in global markets.
items.body:
China's decision to suspend fuel exports for October has raised fresh fears of a further tightening in global markets.
But a combination of rebounding crude oil imports and recent tax cuts on fuel exports makes India well-placed to fill the void.
India has the world's [USN:L4N4070OR TEXT:"fourth-largest refinery system"], with 23 refineries capable of processing roughly 5.6 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil, Indian state data show.
That refining footprint compares with more than 18 million bpd capacity in China and the US and roughly 6.7 million bpd of capacity in Russia, according to the Energy Institute, and traditionally makes India a key fuel supplier to a slew of Asian economies.
India is also the consistently larger fuel exporter compared to China, with India's combined shipments of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel hitting roughly 47 million metric tons in 2025 compared with China's 25.4 million tons, data from Kpler showed.
However, India's combined exports of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel over the first nine months of 2026 have contracted by roughly 23%, or nearly 8 million metric tons, from a year earlier.
The US-Israeli war on Iran has triggered steep cuts to oil supplies from the Middle East since late February, while sparking fuel and oil rationing across most major economies - including India - for the past several months.
The Indian government also raised duties on fuel exports in the wake of the Iran war, ensuring that the country's refiners were dissuaded from shipping too much fuel overseas while domestic supplies were at risk of depletion.
But the outlook for India's fuel exports is starting to brighten following two consecutive [USN:FWN45M14K TEXT:"cuts to fuel-export taxes"], which boost the appeal of steering more fuel onto the export arena.
CLIMBING CRUDE IMPORTS A [USN:L1N45R00B TEXT:"steep rebound in Middle Eastern crude oil exports"] is likely a major driver behind the easing of India's fuel-export taxes.
India has traditionally sourced around 45% to 50% of its crude oil from the Middle East, with around 9.4 million metric tons of Middle Eastern oil arriving in India each month in 2025, Kpler data showed.
But the war in Iran, which kicked off in late February, resulted in India's average oil imports from the Middle East dropping to less than 6 million tons a month from March through July.
That in turn triggered a broader tightening in India's oil reserves and prompted stepped-up oil imports from other origins, which cost more and took longer to reach India's refineries.
Oil flows from the Middle East have now started to recover, however, with deliveries to India in September topping 11.3 million tons, Kpler data showed.
That is India's highest monthly oil haul from the Middle East since February and has restored confidence among Indian officials that fuel exports can start to be elevated again.
KEY DESTINATIONS The top destinations for Indian fuel exports in 2025 were the United Arab Emirates, Australia, Tanzania, Singapore and South Africa, Kpler data showed.
With tanker traffic through and around the Strait of Hormuz still impacted by the Iran conflict, Indian fuel exporters will presumably prioritize shipments to other markets which are not impacted by the war's fallout.
Singapore and Australia are obvious candidates for stepped-up shipments from India over the near term, given their established track records of being regular and reliable buyers of Indian fuels.
But with China expected to be out of the market for the next few weeks at least, Indian fuel sellers will likely also be able to target markets such as Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines, which used to be heavily reliant on China for much of their fuel inputs.
If Indian refiners can successfully step up supplies to needy buyers just as China steps back from the export market, India could establish itself as one of the world's most important marginal suppliers of refined fuels.
That role has traditionally belonged to China, whose vast refining system has long acted as a pressure valve for regional fuel markets.
But Beijing's repeated willingness to curb exports in favour of domestic energy security means that fuel importers can no longer assume Chinese barrels will be available when shortages emerge.
India is increasingly offering an alternative. Its refiners are highly export-oriented, its links with Middle Eastern crude suppliers are strengthening again and policymakers now appear more comfortable with allowing a greater share of fuel production to reach international markets.
China's export suspension may prove temporary. The larger significance is that global fuel markets are being forced to identify who can step in when China steps back.
With crude supplies recovering, export restrictions easing and spare refining capacity available, India looks better positioned than any other country to fill that role.
For fuel consumers across Asia, that could make India more than just a major exporter. It could make India the new swing supplier that helps keep regional energy markets balanced during periods of disruption.
The opinions expressed here are those of the author , a columnist for Reuters.

By Branko Filipovic and Fedja Grulovic
SARAJEVO/BANJA LUKA, Oct 4 (Reuters) – A Bosniak left-leaning moderate, a pro-Russian Serb nationalist and a Croatian nationalist are leading Sunday’s election for Bosnia’s inter-ethnic tripartite presidency, the election commission said early on Monday, based on ballots from 96.31% of polling stations.

The results were largely in line with expectations and with projections by the Poliwave tracking platform, although voter turnout was low at a combined 42.02% in Bosnia’s two entities, the Bosniak-Croat Federation and the Serb Republika Srpska. Voters also cast ballots for the national parliament, alongside regional races in the two entities.

Voter frustration has grown over an economic slowdown, the slow pace of EU entry talks and a lingering political crisis in which ethnically based dominant parties from the two entities have repeatedly stalled decisions by the weak central government that links them.

Show Full Article

Denis Becirovic, a Bosniak of the Social Democratic Party (SDP-BiH) and part of the current tripartite presidency, garnered 26.78% of votes in the Bosniak-Croat Federation, ahead of the candidate for the centre-right Muslim Party of Democratic Action (SDA). The two had been considered favourites in the election.

Also leading in the Bosniak-Croat Federation was newcomer Darijana Filipovic of the nationalist and pro-European Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ-BiH), with 13.89% of the vote.

In Republika Srpska, Zeljka Cvijanovic, an existing member of the tripartite presidency from the Serb and pro-Russian nationalist Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD), secured 55.41% of votes, the election commission said. 

Voting continued in some polling stations after the 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) deadline on Sunday due to delays related to a new electronic balloting system, Bosnia’s Central Election Commission head Jovan Kalaba told reporters in Sarajevo.

The election commission redesigned ballots and introduced new biometric voter identification and electronic scanners, which it said were aimed at curbing voting fraud.

Speaking in Banja Luka, the largest Bosnian Serb city, Milorad Dodik, a separatist and pro-Russian leader of the SNSD who visited Moscow and met Russian President Vladimir Putin last week, said his party’s candidate Savo Minic won the most votes for president of the Republika Srpska entity.

“We have won the member of the (Bosnian) Presidency, and the president of the Republika Srpska. An unexpectedly high result,” Dodik said.

Since the Bosnian war ended in 1995 under the US-brokered Dayton peace accord, the country has been split along ethnic lines into two entities linked by the weak central government and tripartite presidency.

Bosnia, which has struggled to recover from the 1992-95 war, secured EU candidate status in December 2022 and approval to open accession negotiations in 2024. Actual talks have not started, however, because the domestic legislatures have yet to enact core requirements such as bolstering judicial oversight and passing anti-corruption laws.

Borjana Kristo, the deputy head of the Croat HDZ-BiH, said that overall progress could be made through dialogue after the elections.

“Bosnia must make progress solely on the principle of consensus, dialogue, and mutual respect,” she told party supporters, cautioning against rhetoric that would drag the country backwards.

Many voters in the country of 3.4 million people say they want to move beyond divisive rhetoric but its politics have become deadlocked.

The EU and Russia have been vying for influence over Bosnia, with the EU seeking to expand its membership across the Balkans while Russia wants to slow that process down and preserve its influence over the Republika Srpska. 

The US has also sought to bolster its influence in Bosnia, pushing for a $1.5 billion pipeline project to import US liquefied natural gas. The EU has said, however, that the selection of the company for the project lacked competitive transparency, while Washington and Brussels have also clashed over the role of the High Representative, the international peace overseer for the country.

(Writing by Aleksandar Vasovic; reporting by Branko Filipovic in Sarajevo and Fedja Grulovic in Banja Luka; Editing by David Goodman, Emelia Sithole-Matarise, Edmund Klamann and Christian Schmollinger)

Some people have been spending their holiday hunting for fall webworm larvae, an invasive species the Beijing Wildlife Park has dubbed "the forest food monster".

BEIJING: For most families, China's Golden Week holiday is a time to relax, eat well, and visit the country's tourist hot spots.
But at a wildlife park in Beijing, some people have been spending their holiday hunting for fall webworm larvae, an invasive species of caterpillar the park has dubbed "the forest food monster".
Beijing Wildlife Park asked visitors to catch as many of the caterpillars as possible, rewarding those with the heaviest haul with prizes including as many as 10 park tickets. The caterpillar, native to North America, can damage more than 300 plant species, including crops and fruit trees.

More than 310,000 caterpillars with a combined weight of 47.65kg have been caught by about 2,077 people since the competition began on Sep 28, 2026. (Photo: WeChat/Beijing Wildlife Park)

After a crash course on how to spot the larvae, participants spread out across the nearly 223ha park with disposable gloves, plastic containers and chopsticks.

"Call for warriors! Battle the 'forest food monster' and win grand prizes!" read a poster behind a table stacked with containers of crawling caterpillars.
More than 310,000 caterpillars with a combined weight of 47.65kg have been caught by about 2,077 people since the competition began on Sep 28.
The fall webworm is a major pest in China and produces three generations a year. Beijing is currently experiencing peak damage from this year's third generation of larvae, China's Xinhua news agency reported earlier this week, quoting the chief scientist at the Chinese Academy of Forestry.
"(We've) noticed there are a lot of fall webworm larvae around us," said a 35-year-old participant surnamed Cui. "I think the Beijing Wildlife Park activity is very meaningful. It sparks the interest of our children, and (we) can even win a prize at the same time."

items.summary: Schneider Electric a annoncé lundi l'acquisition de 100% du capital du spécialiste des logiciels industriels américian PTC, au prix de 205 dollars (183 euros) par action.
items.body:
Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) a annoncé lundi l'acquisition de 100% du capital du spécialiste des logiciels industriels américian PTC, au prix de 205 dollars (183 euros) par action.
Le fabricant français d'équipements électriques précise dans un communiqué que le but de ce rachat est de créer "une plateforme de logiciels industriels et d’intelligence artificielle de premier plan".
Cette nouvelle acquisition de Schneider vient quelques mois après la conclusion, en juin, d'un accord pour racheter [USN:FWN43213W TEXT:"Cognite Holding"], un fournisseur privé de logiciels d’intelligence artificielle et de données industrielles.
La finalisation de la transaction, évoquée par une source [USN:L8N45R00E TEXT:"peu avant"] son annonce, est prévue d'ici au troisième trimestre 2027. Elle valorise les capitaux propres de PTC à environ 22,6 milliards de dollars (et une valeur d'entreprise de 23,7 milliards de dollars).
Schneider vise de réaliser 250 millions d'euros de synergies de coûts annuelles, reposant sur un plan d'exécution identifié et devant être atteintes d’ici trois ans, ainsi qu'environ 800 millions d’euros de synergies de revenus.

items.title: El ejército de EEUU dice que atacó una embarcación en el Caribe, matando a cuatro personas
items.author: Kanishka Singh
items.creator: Kanishka Singh
items.summary: El ejército de Estados Unidos dijo el domingo de que cuatro personas habían perdido la vida en un ataque a una embarcación en el mar Caribe, el último de una serie de ataques que, según Washington, tienen como objetivo a "narcoterroristas", pero que los expertos en derechos humanos consideran ejecuciones extrajudiciales.
items.body:
El ejército de Estados Unidos dijo el domingo de que cuatro personas habían perdido la vida en un ataque a una embarcación en el mar Caribe, el último de una serie de ataques que, según Washington, tienen como objetivo a "narcoterroristas", pero que los expertos en derechos humanos consideran ejecuciones extrajudiciales.
El Mando Sur de EEUU dijo en la red social X que "llevó a cabo un ataque letal y cinético contra una lancha rápida que operaba a lo largo de rutas establecidas de narcotráfico en el Caribe".
Citó lo que denominó "información de inteligencia confirmada" para alegar la participación activa de la embarcación en el narcotráfico, sin aportar más detalles.
Añadió que cuatro personas, a las que calificó de "narcoterroristas", resultaron muertas.
El Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump ha afirmado que las embarcaciones contra las que ha atacado desde septiembre de 2025 transportaban narcóticos.
Los ataques estadounidenses contra este tipo de embarcaciones en el Caribe y el Pacífico oriental han acabado con la vida de más de 220 personas.
Expertos y defensores de los derechos humanos, tanto en EEUU como en el extranjero, han cuestionado la legalidad de los ataques.
Human Rights Watch, Amnistía Internacional y expertos independientes de la ONU han calificado los ataques de ejecuciones extrajudiciales ilegales.
Ben Saul, relator especial de la ONU sobre derechos humanos y lucha contra el terrorismo, ha afirmado que existen "motivos razonables para creer" que dichos ataques "constituyeron crímenes contra la humanidad por asesinato según el derecho internacional consuetudinario".
La Unión Estadounidense por las Libertades Civiles ha calificado las afirmaciones del Gobierno de Trump contra aquellos a quienes tiene en el punto de mira de "afirmaciones sin fundamento y alarmistas".

items.title: Taipei mayor defends city's inclusivity after gay bar raid sparks protests
items.author: Ben Blanchard, Yimou Lee
items.creator: Ben Blanchard, Yimou Lee
items.summary: Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an on Monday defended the city as welcoming and inclusive after a police raid of a gay bar sparked protests by the LGBTQ+ community over alleged discrimination and official misconduct.
items.body:
Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an on Monday defended the city as welcoming and inclusive after a police raid of a gay bar sparked protests by the LGBTQ+ community over alleged discrimination and official misconduct.
One video of the weekend raid that circulated on social media showed a police officer asking a customer in a wheelchair who was in the toilet how disabled people "manage to have sex in there".
Chiang, who faces reelection next month, said he deeply regretted "improper conduct" by police.
Taiwan legalised same-sex marriage in 2019 in a first for Asia and is normally a bastion of tolerance in a region where LGBTQ+ rights are often suppressed or outlawed. Taipei holds its main Pride event later this month, the largest in East Asia.
Taipei police raided the Commander D bar in the city's main gay neighbourhood of Ximen on Saturday afternoon, citing a complaint alleging the bar could be violating public decency laws. They took 51 people in for questioning and arrested the owner.
Police said on Sunday they had taken disciplinary action against officers for "inappropriate conduct" during the operation, without elaborating.
Chiang, who has previously attended Taipei Pride, said regardless of age, gender, sexual orientation, identity, ethnicity or beliefs, the government must ensure everyone in Taipei enjoys equal rights.
"Taipei has always been an inclusive and friendly city for us," he said.
Chiang, of the opposition Kuomintang, is locked in a tight election race against Puma Shen of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party.
Shen said in a Facebook post on Monday that while any illegality should be handled according to the law, people's rights and dignity should be respected.
"Taipei's diversity and inclusivity should not only be visible on Pride parade day," he wrote.
RIGHTS GROUPS ANGERED The Commander D raid was one of three operations on Saturday involving Ximen gay bars, police precinct spokesperson Chen Yu-cheng told Reuters. Police had in the past conducted "irregular inspections" of the three venues, he said.
Chen added that the precinct inspected 15 entertainment venues on Saturday.
Rights groups say there is a deeper problem.
"This was not a case of individual officers misspeaking or a single instance of excessive enforcement, but the resurfacing of long-standing homophobia, discrimination and abuse of power within the police enforcement system," the Taiwan Alliance to Promote Civil Partnership Rights said in a joint statement with other groups condemning the raid.
One person among the 51 taken in for questioning said they had been detained for more than six hours after police accused them of violating a law that prohibits "wantonly exposing one's naked body or presenting a lascivious posture in a public place."
The person, who requested anonymity, said they had removed their shirt only shortly before police arrived because the bar was crowded and hot.
"I trusted the police to know the law," the person said. "So when they told me I had broken the law by not wearing a shirt in a public place and had to pay a fine, I did not challenge them."
Lead investigator Chen Yi-kai told Reuters shirtless people were taken in because officers had found evidence of sexual or obscene conduct but could not immediately determine who was involved, adding that police were inclined not to fine the 51 people.

items.title: Ifo: Stimmung in der deutschen Autoindustrie sackt ab - "In der Krise"
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Die Stimmung in der deutschen Automobilindustrie hat sich im September stark eingetrübt. Das Barometer für das Geschäftsklima fiel auf minus 35,0 Punkte, von minus 22,0 Zählern im August, wie das Münchner Ifo-Institut am Montag zu seiner Umfrage mitteilte. Die Unternehmen bewerteten ihre Geschäftslage so schlecht wie noch nie in diesem Jahr. Die Aussichten für die kommenden Monate waren schon im August drastisch gesunken und verharrten nun auf tiefem Niveau. "Die Automobilindustrie steckt weiterhin in der Krise", sagte Ifo-Branchenexpertin Anita Wölfl.
items.body:
Die Stimmung in der deutschen Automobilindustrie hat sich im September stark eingetrübt. Das Barometer für das Geschäftsklima fiel auf minus 35,0 Punkte, von minus 22,0 Zählern im August, wie das Münchner Ifo-Institut am Montag zu seiner Umfrage mitteilte. Die Unternehmen bewerteten ihre Geschäftslage so schlecht wie noch nie in diesem Jahr. Die Aussichten für die kommenden Monate waren schon im August drastisch gesunken und verharrten nun auf tiefem Niveau. "Die Automobilindustrie steckt weiterhin in der Krise", sagte Ifo-Branchenexpertin Anita Wölfl.
Diese Krisenstimmung lässt sich an vielen weiteren Indikatoren erkennen: So sackten die Exporterwartungen in der Autoindustrie ab, nachdem sie zuvor noch gestiegen waren. Ähnliches galt für die Beschäftigungserwartungen. Die Unternehmen bewerteten im September überdies ihren Auftragsbestand erneut schlechter als im Vormonat. Die Ertragslage, die immer vierteljährlich abgefragt wird, ist den Unternehmensangaben zufolge im dritten Quartal im Vergleich zum Vorquartal deutlich gesunken.
In anderen Industriezweigen wie der Elektro- und der Chemieindustrie hat sich die Stimmung zuletzt merklich aufgehellt. Ein Grund für die Schwäche der Autobranche ist die wachsende Konkurrenz aus China, etwa bei Elektrofahrzeugen. Die chinesischen Autobauer drängen mit Macht auf den europäischen Markt, weil der eigene Markt schwächelt und es eine enorme Überproduktion gibt. Der US-Markt ist ihnen aufgrund der Handelspolitik versperrt. Die deutsche Autoindustrie lehnt deshalb Importzölle nicht mehr generell ab. Priorität müsse aber weiter die Stärkung der eigenen Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und ein Dialog mit China als Handelspartner haben, erklärte die Chefin des Verbandes der Automobilindustrie (VDA), Hildegard Müller, kürzlich.

FAST

Oct 5 : France's Schneider Electric said on Monday it had agreed to buy PTC in an all-cash deal valuing the US software company's equity at around $22.6 billion, confirming reports from Sunday.
The $205-per-share offer implies an enterprise value of $23.7 billion for Boston-based PTC and represents a 42.3 per cent premium to its last closing share price.
The deal will be financed through a combination of equity and new debt issuance and is expected to be closed in the third quarter of 2027.
The acquisition would deepen the French engineering company's push into software acquisitions, having agreed to buy Cognite Holding, a privately held provider of AI software and industrial data, in June.

Schneider, once known primarily for industrial components like fuses and circuit breakers, now builds the backbone of data centres, supplying everything from cooling units and server racks to critical power distribution equipment.
The booming demand for data centres, particularly from the United States, is driving Schneider's earnings, offering a growing source of revenue helping offset weakness in some traditional electrical-equipment markets.
PTC, which provides software solutions for designing, manufacturing and servicing products across multiple sectors, has also benefited from growing demand for its AI-powered tools.
In July, Schneider Electric lifted its annual revenue forecast after reporting record first-half results, betting on strong demand for its core industrial software and artificial intelligence-powered tools.

items.title: カタール、ユーロクリアと連携　国債・イスラム債市場を世界に開放へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
[ロンドン ５日 ロイター] - カタール中央銀行と証券決済機関のユーロクリアは５日、カタールが自国通貨建て国債やイスラム債についてユーロクリアと清算・決済の連携体制を構築し、より多くの国際投資家に対して市場を開放すると発表した。

両機関は共同声明の中で、この取り組みにより流動性が向上し、市場の効率性が改善され、カタールへの国際的な資本流入がさらに拡大すると見込まれると述べた。

• この措置により、世界中の投資家は、ユーロクリアの国際決済システムを通じて、対象となるカタール・リヤル建ての国債および「スクーク」として知られるイスラム債を購入、保有、決済できるようになる。

• ベルギーに拠点を置くユーロクリアは、証券決済および保管サービスを提供することで、銀行や投資家が金融資産を保有、移転、決済できるようにしている。

• 新興市場の現地通貨建て債に対する投資家の需要は高まっている。

•

• 新たな体制の下、ユーロクリア・バンクが国際決済サービスを提供する一方、カタールの中央証券保管機関であるＥＤＡＡは引き続き国内投資家へのサービスを提供する。証券の発行および投資家への支払いについては、引き続きカタール中銀が責任を負う。

items.title: 中国当局の指示で台湾総統の息子を監視か、米FBIが女を逮捕
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
米連邦捜査局（FBI）は4日、中国当局者の指示で台湾総統の息子を監視した疑いで、カリフォルニア州在住のワンイン・チャン容疑者（34）を逮捕したと発表した。
FBIは中国へ出発する予定だったチャン容疑者をロサンゼルス国際空港で逮捕した。当局は、未登録で外国政府の代理人として活動した罪で訴追した。
FBIによると、チャン容疑者は台湾の頼清徳総統の息子を監視していた。FBIは監視対象の氏名を直接明らかにしなかったが、その後、米国在住の頼廷宇氏だとする米紙ニューヨーク・ポストの記事を共有した。
台湾総統府は、チャン容疑者の行為を「越境弾圧の典型例」とし、台湾市民を保護した米政府に謝意を表明した。

items.body:
Alle europäischen Autobauer schaffen einer Studie zufolge die CO2-Grenzwerte der Europäischen Union. Schon jetzt hätten die Hersteller die Vorgaben zu 75 Prozent erfüllt, hieß es in einer Studie der Lobbyorganisation Transport & Environment, die am Montag veröffentlicht wurde. Für die vollständige Umsetzung haben sie bis Ende 2027 Zeit. Es sei damit zu rechnen, dass viele Hersteller schon vor Ablauf der Frist zum Ziel kämen.
"Die Anzeichen sind klar: Die CO2–Ziele funktionieren so wie erwartet", hieß es in der Untersuchung. Frühere Aussagen aus der Branche, dass die Vorgaben nicht erreicht werden könnten, hätten sich als falsch erwiesen. "Das Schlussquartal 2026 wird für die europäische Branche der Schlüsselmoment." Jetzt kämen die Verhandlungen zu den CO2-Zielen zum Abschluss. Die Verantwortlichen müssten entscheiden, ob die elektrische Zukunft Europas gesichert werde oder mit Alternativen wie Biofuels eine Sackgasse eingeschlagen werde. "Die Politiker müssen entschieden handeln, um die Bevölkerung zu schützen und diese zur letzten fossilen Energie-Krise zu machen."
In den vergangenen Monaten schnellte der Absatz von Elektroautos in vielen europäischen Ländern nach oben. Dabei spielten die hohen Ölpreise und staatliche Kaufanreize eine wichtige Rolle. Dazu kommt eine zunehmende Auswahl insbesondere bei kleineren Fahrzeugen. Der Verkauf von Autos zum Preis von weniger als 25.000 Euro dürfte sich im laufenden Jahr um das Siebenfache im Vergleich zu 2024 erhöhen, hieß es in der T&E-Studie. Zuletzt hatte Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) den elektrischen Polo und drei Schwestermodelle in dieser Kategorie auf den Markt gebracht. Allerdings seien weiter mehr Verbrennerfahrzeuge in dieser Preiskategorie verfügbar.
Überhaupt sei das laufende Jahr geprägt von einer Vielzahl neuer Fahrzeuge. Derzeit seien mehr als 150 Elektromodelle auf dem Markt, fast 40 davon seien in der ersten Jahreshälfte eingeführt worden. Angeführt werde diese Statistik von den europäischen Autobauern, die fast 60 Prozent der Fahrzeuge stellten. Chinesische Hersteller kämen auf 21 Prozent.
items.raw_description: Alle europäischen Autobauer schaffen einer Studie zufolge die CO2-Grenzwerte der Europäischen Union. Schon jetzt hätten die Hersteller die Vorgaben zu 75 Prozent erfüllt, hieß es in einer Studie der Lobbyorganisation Transport & Environment, die am Montag veröffentlicht wurde. Für die vollständige Umsetzung haben sie bis Ende 2027 Zeit. Es sei damit zu rechnen, dass viele Hersteller schon vor Ablauf der Frist zum Ziel kämen.

items.title: Brazil election: Why Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro are headed for a high-stakes runoff
items.author: Bhanu Pratap
items.summary: Brazil election: Brazil’s presidential election is headed for a runoff between incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro after neither candidate secured more than 50% of the first-round vote.
items.body: Brazilians voted on Sunday in a high-stakes presidential election that pitted incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, as the country’s political battle unfolded amid a broader rightward shift across Latin America.Neither candidate secured more than 50% of the vote in the first round, sending Lula and Bolsonaro into a runoff scheduled for October 25, as per Reuters.Nearly 159 million eligible voters also cast ballots for 27 state governors, all 513 members of the lower house of Congress, 54 of the 81 senators and members of state legislatures, the report said.Polling stations closed at 5 pm, with voters still in line allowed to cast their ballots.Flavio Bolsonaro exceeds expectationsFlavio Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, performed better than expected in the first round compared with earlier polls and finished with a narrow lead over Lula, setting up a closely fought runoff.The election was shaped by concerns over the cost of living, corruption and public security, while the contest also reflected a wider ideological divide playing out across Latin America.Right-wing parties aligned with US President Donald Trump have made gains in several countries in the region, including Argentina, Colombia, Honduras and Peru, according to Reuters.Flavio Bolsonaro has sought to emphasize his ties with the Trump administration.He has denied receiving assistance from the US government and has campaigned on tougher action against criminal groups, closer ties with the White House and better trade arrangements, including in the rare-minerals sector.He has also pledged to seek the release of his father and bring him back into political life.Lula seeks a fourth termLula, 80, is contesting his seventh presidential election and seeking another term after returning to office in 2023.His government has strengthened ties with Beijing. The president has increasingly made resistance to US pressure a campaign issue, particularly after the Trump administration imposed high tariffs on Brazilian exports, revoked the visa of Brazil’s ambassador and sanctioned a Supreme Court justice involved in the investigation that eventually led to Jair Bolsonaro’s conviction.Lula’s approval ratings have also fallen during his third term.After voting, Lula said that, if re-elected, he would need to “do double of what we have done” and expressed confidence that he could win in the first round, according to Reuters.But the election has proved more difficult than expected for the incumbent, amid concerns over affordability and a corruption scandal that also involved the judge who led the investigation into Bolsonaro.Bolsonaro campaigns on crime, securityFor Bolsonaro, crime and public security have been central campaign issues.Bolsonaro is also facing corruption allegations, including claims that he received millions of dollars from a disgraced banker to allegedly produce a film about his father’s life, according to reports.Lula’s supporters have pointed to his social welfare programmes and his resistance to pressure from Washington as key reasons to back him in the runoff.The incumbent has sought to portray his government as a defender of Brazil’s economic interests while highlighting policies aimed at reducing poverty and inequality.The October 25 runoff will force Brazilian voters to choose between keeping Lula in office and returning the country to the right under Flavio Bolsonaro.
items.raw_description: Brazil election: Brazil’s presidential election is headed for a runoff between incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro after neither candidate secured more than 50% of the first-round vote.

items.title: Russian air strikes targeted port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, governor says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Massive Russian air strikes targeted industrial and port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, Governor Oleh Kiper said on the Telegram messaging app on Monday.
items.body:
Massive Russian air strikes targeted industrial and port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, Governor Oleh Kiper said on the Telegram messaging app on Monday.
All of the fires caused have been extinguished so far, he added.
A Russian air strike on Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-biggest city, killed one person and injured six others, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said on Telegram late on Sunday.
The Russian defence ministry said on Telegram it hit Vylkove port, fuel depot facilities in Chornomorsk and cargo vessels, all in the Odesa region, as well as a power station in the Kharkiv region, which it said were used for military purposes.

items.title: イエメン一部地域で4世帯に3世帯が食料不足、戦闘激化で＝ＷＦＰ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Olivia Le Poidevin

[ジュネーブ ２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Olivia Le Poidevin

[ジュネーブ ２日 ロイター] - 国連世界食糧計画（ＷＦＰ）は２日、イエメンの一部地域で４世帯に３世帯が十分な食料を得られずにいると明らかにした。戦闘激化で数万人が避難を余儀なくされ、数百万人への物資供給が滞っており、影響は「極めて壊滅的」になりかねないと警告した。

イエメンでは、２０２２年に国連が仲介した停戦で越境攻撃がほぼ停止して以降、サウジアラビアと親イラン武装組織フーシ派の間で戦闘が最も激しくなっている。 

ＷＦＰのマシュー・ホリングワース事務局次長（プログラム運営担当）は記者団に対し、ＷＦＰがアクセス可能な政府支配地域では、戦闘により、十分な食料を得られない世帯の割合がわずか数週間で７４％に上昇したと述べた。政府支配地域全体の人口は約１０００万人と推計される。 

ホリングワース氏は「今回の治安悪化が食料安全保障の状況に及ぼす影響は、極めて壊滅的なものになる恐れがある」と警告した。

「この状況が続けば、飢餓危機はさらに深刻化するだろう」と指摘。タイズなど前線地域では戦闘により、支援を届けることがますます難しくなっていると述べた。 

ＷＦＰは支援を拡大しているが、数週間以内に約１億０９００万ドルの資金を確保できなければ、新たに国内で避難した１５万２０００人と、既に支援している１４０万人への食料と資金が底を突くとしている。

items.title: Takaichi pledges fiscal discipline as Japan's debt bill rises
items.author: Leika Kihara
items.creator: Leika Kihara
items.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields.
items.body:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields.
She said the government would pursue fiscal sustainability even as it ramps up spending to bolster growth potential, including by reviewing existing tax breaks and subsidies.
"Fiscal sustainability is obviously a prerequisite in pursuing our 'responsible and proactive' fiscal policy," Takaichi said in a policy speech to parliament.
The remarks reflect mounting concern in Tokyo over rising Japanese government bond (JGB) yields, which would boost the cost of funding the premier's ambitious spending plans.
The 30-year JGB yield hit a record high of 4.235% on Monday on jitters over the risk of increased debt issuance and inflation worries fuelled by the Middle East war.
Japan's public debt, at roughly twice the size of its economy, is the largest in the developed world. Funding costs are climbing as the Bank of Japan raises interest rates and tapers bond purchases in an effort to wean the economy off decades of massive stimulus.
Takaichi said the government will seek to draw in private investment in growth areas through "massive, long-term fiscal expenditure deployed in a well-planned, predictable manner."
At the same time, it would keep a lid on annual bond issuance, calibrating borrowing to tax revenues, interest rates, debt-financing costs and economic and market developments, the premier said in the speech to an extraordinary parliament session that convened on Monday.
"If the economy and markets make unexpected moves, we will scrutinise their impact and respond nimbly as needed," she added without elaborating.
Fiscal policy is set to take centre stage in parliamentary debate in Japan as rising concerns over the fiscal health of advanced economies fuel a broader rise in global bond yields.
The administration's immediate priority is passing legislation backing Takaichi's plan for a [USN:L1N457045 TEXT:"two-year tax cut"] on food items from next April, which sparked a bond selloff due to a lack of detail on how the revenue shortfall will be filled.
The government is also preparing next year's budget, with ministries seeking record levels of spending.
Separately, Takaichi said Tokyo will set aside multi-year funds for strategically important economic security initiatives.
"We will implement policies steadily, get things done one by one, and communicate them carefully to the public and markets," Takaichi said.

items.body:
The Russian defence ministry said on Monday its forces struck two Ukrainian cargo vessels in the Black Sea.
It said it hit fuel storage facilities at the port of Chornomorsk that were intended to supply Ukrainian armed forces, as well as a dry cargo vessel carrying military equipment.
Another dry cargo vessel transporting military supplies was hit south of the city of Odesa, according to a statement. It also said the Kochetok electrical substation was struck in the Kharkiv region.

items.title: 豪当局、フライドバイ副操縦士の同国との関連捜査　国内の大学に在籍記録
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Praveen Menon　Alexander Cornwell

[シドニー／テルアビブ ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Praveen Menon　Alexander Cornwell

[シドニー／テルアビブ ４日 ロイター] - オーストラリア連邦警察の報道官は４日、フライドバイＦＺ１０７３便の機長を刺し機体の乗っ取りを図った副操縦士について、複数機関で構成する豪州の対テロ部隊が同国との関係を捜査していると明らかにした。

オーストラリア連邦警察の報道官によると、連邦警察、ビクトリア州警察、情報機関のオーストラリア保安情報機構（ＡＳＩＯ）で構成される「ビクトリア州対テロ合同チーム」が「同副操縦士とオーストラリアとの関連」を調べている。

捜査について説明を受けた関係者２人によると、副操縦士はかつてビクトリア州の州都メルボルンの大学で学んでいた。別の関係者は、約１０年前にＲＭＩＴ大学で学んでいたと述べた。同大学は短い声明で、副操縦士が在籍していたことを認めたが、工学分野の資格は取得していないと説明した。氏名や在籍時期は明らかにしなかった。

関係者２人によると、副操縦士はオマーン国籍のハマム・アルハンマミ容疑者とされる。イスラエル当局者は副操縦士の名前を明らかにしていないが、オマーン出身だとしている。ＵＡＥ当局とフライドバイは、副操縦士の身元を公表していない。

ＵＡＥは同容疑者に対する正式な訴追を発表しておらず、弁護人を選任しているかどうかも不明。オマーンも事件についてコメントしていない。

墜落の惨事を免れたＦＺ１０７３便 には非番のフライドバイ操縦士が乗り合わせており、この操縦士が操縦を引き継いでサウジアラビア北西部のタブーク空港に着陸させた。副操縦士はサウジ当局に拘束された後、１０月１日にＵＡＥへ移送された。

英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）は４日、捜査に詳しい関係者２人の情報として、アルハンマミ容疑者がオーストラリア滞在中に過激派のモスクや過激派のウェブサイトを訪れていた疑いがあると報じた。ＦＴによると、オーストラリア情報機関は容疑者に関する記録を保有していたという。

items.title: マクロスコープ：高市首相の所信表明、「機動的」に浮かぶ腐心の跡
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Tamiyuki Kihara　Yoshifumi Takemoto

[東京 ５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Tamiyuki Kihara　Yoshifumi Takemoto

[東京 ５日 ロイター] - 臨時国会が５日に召集され、高市早苗首相が所信表明演説に臨んだ。財政政策を訴える場面が目立つ中、政府与党内で注目を集めたのが「機動的な対応」という言葉だ。複数の関係者によると、高市氏は「リフレ論者」というイメージを払拭したい一方、自身が必要と考える財政出動はためらわない姿勢も崩していない。双方のバランスを考えた末にたどり着いた表現だという。

＜「経済財政運営上、当然のこと」＞

「経済や市場が想定と異なる動きを示した場合には、その影響を十分に分析し、必要な対応を機動的に講じる」。高市氏は演説の序盤、自らが掲げる「責任ある積極財政」に関連してこう述べた。債務残高の対国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比を安定的に引き下げるという目標も改めて強調。「経済、物価、税収、金利、利払い費、市場の状況」などを総合的に検証し、通年の国債発行額を「適切にコントロールしていく」とも語った。

高市氏が考える「機動的な対応」とは何か。首相官邸幹部は「市場の動向や外部環境の変化を見ながら対応するということだ」と説明する。「基本的な方向性を示しつつ、起こり得る状況に機動的に対応するのは、経済財政運営上、当然のこと」とも話したが、具体的にどのような手法を想定しているかは明言を避けた。

国債をめぐっては、高市氏が８月の読売新聞のインタビューで、来年度一般会計の新規国債発行額を４０兆円程度に抑えるとも取れる発言をして以降、政府内でも同規模を想定する見方が広がっている。ただ、高市氏は今回の演説で具体的な金額に触れなかった。前出の官邸幹部は「通年の国債発行額を適切に管理する。予算編成改革の大きな枠組みのなかでやっていく」と説明したが、規模については「現時点では踏み込んでいない」と述べるにとどめた。

＜「マーケットが跳ねるのを警戒している」＞

政府は夏以降、「高市氏はリフレ論者ではない」（片山さつき財務相）と繰り返し発信している。高市氏は２月の施政方針演説で「長年続いてきた過度な緊縮志向、未来への投資不足の流れを断ち切る」と宣言し、あわせて「財政の持続可能性を実現し、マーケットからの信認を確保していく」と述べていた。当時は強気な姿勢が目立ったが、今回の演説は全体として穏当な表現にとどまった。

複数の政府関係者への取材から、演説に込めた高市氏の考えが浮かび上がる。官邸に出入りする関係者の一人は、高市氏が市場の動きを強く意識していると明かし、「これから進める政策によってマーケットが跳ねるのを警戒している」と話す。その一方で、高市氏は支持層が期待する「積極財政」の路線にもこだわっているという。同関係者は、各方面に配慮した結果、「機動的な対応」や「国債発行額の適切なコントロール」といった、どちらにも解釈できる表現に落ち着いたとの見方を示した。

また、財政政策に携わる別の関係者は、「機動的な対応」はあくまで「経済や市場」が想定と異なる動きを見せた場合のものだと強調。長期金利や為替の動きへの対応に加え、「経済状況が悪化した際には必要に応じて財政を吹かすとの考えが込められている」とも解説した。

＜「見ているところがまったく違う」＞

ただ、政府内には「市場の信認は具体的な数字を示して初めて得られるものだ」（経済官庁幹部）との声が根強い。年末にかけては防衛費増額の議論や来年度当初予算案の編成が控える。高市氏がどう市場の信認を得ていくのか、与党内や専門家の間では期待と疑問が入り交じっている。

野村証券の岩下真理エグゼクティブ金利ストラテジストは、高市氏が口にした「機動的な対応」に注目し、「機動的という言葉を使うのは政権として初めてだ。市場の信認を得るため、いままでにない言葉を使っている」と分析。「高市政権が今後、マーケットにどれだけ配慮した政策を取るのか期待したい」と語った。

食料品の消費税減税など、政権の財政政策に懐疑的な見方を示してきた自民党の政務三役経験者は、自国の金利上昇を懸念する米政府との関係もあり、高市氏が夏以降「明らかに市場に配慮し始めている」と指摘する。今回の演説からもその「配慮」がうかがえると評価した。

一方、ＳＢＩ証券の道家映二チーフ債券ストラテジストは、「金融市場は具体的な政策の中身を見るので、言葉だけを信じることはない」と話す。財源をめぐる議論が先送りされ続けている点に触れ、「国債発行額でうわべの数字合わせのようなことをしても市場は信じない」と強調した。現時点では、政権の財政政策にほとんど変化はないとの見方を示した。「市場関係者は高市政権を誤解しているのではない。見ているところが政権とはまったく違うということだ」

（鬼原民幸、竹本能文　編集：橋本浩）

items.title: 高市首相、「市場が想定と異なる動き示せば機動的に対応」 所信表明で財政規律に配慮
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Yoshifumi Takemoto

[東京 ５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Yoshifumi Takemoto

[東京 ５日 ロイター] -  高市早苗首相は５日召集の臨時国会で所信表明演説に臨み、看板政策の「責任ある積極財政」について、経済成長の重要性を改めて訴えるとともに財政規律も重視する姿勢を示した。国債発行額を制御するほか、市場が想定外の動きを示した場合は「必要な対応を機動的に講じる」と述べ、政権発足以降に進んだ円安・金利上昇に対する配慮を前面に出した。

高市氏は「責任ある積極財政」の説明に一定の時間を割いた。国内投資を引き出して「ＧＤＰ（国内総生産）拡大下での好循環」を実現すると主張する一方、「政府が単に歳出を増やすということではない」、「強い経済と財政の持続可能性をともに実現する、新しい経済財政運営を始める」と訴えた。

財政の持続可能性は「当然の前提」とした上で、債務残高の対ＧＤＰ比を安定的に引き下げる目標を中核に位置付けるとした。プライマリーバランス（基礎的財政収支、ＰＢ）は複数年度で管理し、「経済成長がもたらす効果も踏まえ、経済、物価、税収、金利、利払い費、市場の状況などを総合的に検証しながら、通年の国債発行額を適切にコントロールする」と述べた。

高市氏の経済政策に対し、金利上昇と為替の円安で反応しがちな金融市場との対話に力を入れる方針も示した。「経済や市場が想定と異なる動きを示した場合には、その影響を十分に分析し、必要な対応を機動的に講じる」、「政策を着実に実行し、一つ一つ確かな結果を積み上げ、その内容を国民や国内外の市場関係者に丁寧に説明する。高市内閣は、正攻法で、市場の政府に対する信頼を高めていく」などと語った。

臨時国会で関連法案が焦点となる飲食料品の消費税減税については、「家計に少しでもゆとりを生み出したい」と狙いを説明。財源は「市場の信認を得られるよう、特例公債に頼らずに確保することとしており、御心配には及ばない」と述べた。

人工知能（ＡＩ）など１７分野で２０４０年度までに累計３７０兆円超の官民投資を進める成長戦略は、今後５年間の国内投資の道筋を示す「日本成長戦略実行計画」を年内に策定するとした。「必要な投資は先送りしない」とする一方、「費用対効果を継続的に検証し、見直しを行い、効果の乏しい事業を漫然と続けることはしない」と語った。

また、ホルムズ海峡封鎖など中東産原油の調達難を念頭に、「調達先の多角化とリスク分散を徹底することにより、エネルギー調達基盤を抜本的に強化するための制度を整備する」ことを明らかにした。

外交と安全保障では、台湾有事を巡る昨年１１月の国会答弁以降に関係が冷え込む中国に言及。「重要な隣国であり、課題がある中にも長年の積み重ねがある」とし、「戦略的互恵関係を包括的に推進する」と述べた。東シナ海や南シナ海の問題、人権上の懸念、日本人の安全など「主張すべきは主張」すると同時に、「建設的かつ安定的な関係を構築する」とした。

米国が批判する 国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）など国際裁判所への支持を改めて打ち出したものの、ＩＣＣの赤根智子所長が米国の制裁対象になったことには触れなかった。

items.title: New Zealand's Bracewell shifts to casual contract, eyes BBL opportunity
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: New Zealand all-rounder Michael Bracewell will move to a casual contract for the 2026-27 season as he pursues an opportunity in Australia's Big Bash League, the country's cricket board (NZC) said on Monday.
items.body:
New Zealand all-rounder Michael Bracewell will move to a casual contract for the 2026-27 season as he pursues an opportunity in Australia's Big Bash League, the country's cricket board (NZC) said on Monday.
Bracewell, who has played 105 times for New Zealand across all three formats, will feature in the limited-overs series against India beginning this month.
The 35-year-old joins [USN:L4N4500JN TEXT:"Mark Chapman"], Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson, Adam Milne and Tim Seifert among players who have opted for the casual contract system, which allows them to play in high-paying Twenty20 leagues while remaining available for national duty.
"As a white-ball only player, this felt like too good of an opportunity to pass up," Bracewell said in a statement.
"I'm still very much committed to the Black Caps and can't wait to be involved in the upcoming India tour and future white-ball series."
Batter Nick Kelly will replace Bracewell on NZC's central contract list.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Takahiko Wada

［東京　５日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Takahiko Wada

［東京　５日　ロイター］ - 日銀は５日、４―６月期の需給ギャップがプラス０．５５％になったと発表した。１―３月期のプラス０．３６％を上回り、２０２４年７―９月期以降、８四半期連続でプラスとなった。需要超の状況の持続は物価に上昇圧力が掛かっていることを示し、日銀の利上げ継続をサポートする要因になる。

需給ギャップは、日本経済の潜在的な供給力と実際の需要の差を示す。内訳は、資本投入ギャップがプラス０．３３％、労働投入ギャップがプラス０．２２％。

国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）から推計する内閣府に対し、日銀は生産設備の稼働率や失業率・労働参加率などから試算している。

併せて発表した潜在成長率はプラス０．８１％。２５年度下半期のプラス０．８０％を小幅に上回った。

items.title: ¿Qué está en juego para la economía de Brasil y su relación con Trump en la segunda vuelta?
items.author: Daniel Carvalho, Beatriz Reis, Simone Iglesias
items.summary: Brasil enfrenta un déficit fiscal cercano al 10% del PIB, deuda superior al 80% y tasas de interés elevadas, mientras los inversores esperan señales sobre las políticas económicas del próximo gobierno ...
items.body: Bloomberg — Flávio Bolsonaro se situó de forma sorprendente por delante de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en la primera vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil, lo que le convierte en el claro favorito para ganar la segunda vuelta y llevar a este país, uno de los más importantes de América Latina, hacia la extrema derecha. Con sus aliados conservadores dominando en todo Brasil en las urnas este domingo, Bolsonaro cerró la jornada obteniendo alrededor del 47% de los votos frente al 45% aproximadamente del izquierdista Lula, con el recuento casi completado. Ver más: Flávio Bolsonaro disputará con ventaja sobre Lula segunda vuelta de la elección presidencial de Brasil Se enfrentarán el 25 de octubre, pero es probable que al veterano presidente, que se presenta a la que probablemente sea su última campaña, le resulte difícil recortar la diferencia, dado que se espera que la mayor parte del apoyo de los candidatos eliminados se decante por Bolsonaro. Se prevé que los activos brasileños se disparen cuando abran los mercados el lunes, ante los indicios de que Bolsonaro se encamina hacia la victoria. Los inversores han respaldado en gran medida al hijo mayor del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, al considerarlo más propenso a aplicar políticas que aborden el deterioro de la situación fiscal de Brasil. La contienda entrará ahora en tres semanas frenéticas de campaña para determinar quién controlará la mayor economía de América Latina, un resultado relevante para los intentos del presidente Donald Trump de ejercer el dominio de EE.UU. sobre el hemisferio occidental. Lula se ha resistido a los esfuerzos de la administración estadounidense, mientras que Bolsonaro desea acercarse a la órbita de Trump. El ambiente en la sede de la campaña de Bolsonaro en Brasilia era festivo a última hora del domingo, con una barbacoa en marcha y la música a todo volumen, según una persona presente, mientras que los colaboradores de Lula afirmaron que su campaña se vio sorprendida por la magnitud de los resultados por encima de lo esperado de su rival. Bolsonaro, lleno de confianza, declaró “el fin de la era del Partido de los Trabajadores” en sus primeras declaraciones, proclamando que él y sus aliados habían asestado un golpe definitivo al movimiento de izquierdas que Lula había construido, pasando de ser un valiente advenedizo a convertirse en la fuerza política más dominante de Brasil. Ver más: “El partido está por comenzar”, dice Lula; Flávio afirma que hará una campaña “limpia” “Podremos construir un gobierno inspirado en el de mi padre, una administración incluso mejor que la suya”, afirmó Bolsonaro en un discurso a puerta cerrada, según un vídeo al que tuvo acceso Bloomberg News. Lula, por su parte, intentó mantener la confianza de sus seguidores, expresando su seguridad en su capacidad para la segunda vuelta y afirmando que el lunes comienza una nueva campaña. “La segunda vuelta es nuestra oportunidad de mostrar la verdadera imagen del Brasil actual y el Brasil que queremos», declaró Lula en São Paulo. Pero para ganar, el presidente de 80 años, que gobernó Brasil de 2003 a 2010, fue posteriormente a prisión por condenas por corrupción que finalmente fueron anuladas y luego volvió a ocupar el cargo más alto del Estado, tendrá que lograr otra remontada sin precedentes. Desde que Brasil recuperó la democracia en 1989, ningún candidato que quedara rezagado en la primera vuelta ha ganado la segunda vuelta. Incluso si lo consigue, los resultados iniciales han asestado un golpe devastador al Partido de los Trabajadores, que ha ganado cinco de las últimas seis elecciones presidenciales, pero que ahora se enfrenta a nuevas pruebas de que su mensaje ya no cala entre los brasileños como lo hacía antes. Aparte de Bolsonaro, la derecha brasileña obtuvo avances sustanciales en el Senado y en las elecciones clave a gobernador. Es probable que esto refuerce el poder del senador de 45 años para reformar las instituciones brasileñas, incluido el Tribunal Supremo que condenó a su padre por conspirar para dar un golpe de Estado tras perder las elecciones de 2022 frente a Lula, en caso de que se imponga en la segunda vuelta. La magnitud del éxito de la derecha llevó a los asesores de Lula a concluir que los votantes habían expresado un rechazo más amplio al Partido de los Trabajadores que iba más allá del descontento con el presidente, según dos de ellos que hablaron bajo condición de anonimato. Ver más: Aliados de Bolsonaro ganan fuerza en Senado de Brasil y se acercan a mayoría contra el Tribunal Supremo Y, sin embargo, este revés también obligará al partido a reconocer su incapacidad para formar una cantera de candidatos capaces de suceder a su veterano líder. El partido “se enfrentará a un balance no solo sobre la sucesión de Lula, y la falta de nuevos líderes, sino también sobre su desconexión con la mayoría de los votantes en muchas prioridades sociales y económicas”, afirmó Mario Braga, analista geopolítico de la consultora RANE. Las repercusiones de las elecciones se extenderán mucho más allá de Brasil. Una victoria de Bolsonaro aceleraría los esfuerzos de Trump por reafirmar la primacía de EE.UU. en las Américas, tras las recientes victorias de aliados conservadores en Colombia, Chile y Perú. Brasil, bajo el mandato de Lula, ha sido uno de los últimos bastiones que se han resistido a la denominada “Doctrina Donroe” de Trump para el hemisferio occidental, manteniéndose como un referente del acercamiento regional a China que el líder estadounidense está tratando de revertir. Trump ha desempeñado un papel desmesurado en la política del país desde el año pasado, cuando impuso aranceles a Brasil en un intento infructuoso de ayudar a Jair Bolsonaro a eludir una condena. Posteriormente se reconcilió con Lula y levantó los aranceles. Sin embargo, volvió a imponerlos en julio, lo que brindó a Lula la oportunidad de argumentar que Trump estaba interfiriendo en los asuntos brasileños para impulsar a Flávio Bolsonaro, quien se ha comprometido a acercar el país a EE.UU. La campaña electoral brasileña, sin embargo, se ha centrado en gran medida en otro motivo de preocupación para los votantes: la corrupción, avivada principalmente por una investigación sobre el Banco Master SA, la entidad crediticia en quiebra que se encuentra en el centro de una investigación por fraude de US$10.000 millones y que ha trastocado repetidamente el curso de la campaña. Ver más: ETF brasileño en Tokio sube casi 8% con ventaja de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre Lula Bolsonaro se quedó rezagado respecto a Lula a principios de este año tras revelarse que había solicitado dinero a Daniel Vorcaro, el antiguo propietario del banco que se encuentra en prisión, para una película sobre su padre, vínculos que ahora son objeto de una investigación federal. Bolsonaro niega haber cometido irregularidad alguna. Sin embargo, el escándalo acabó por minar posteriormente la campaña de reelección de Lula, después de que la filtración de mensajes pusiera de manifiesto los estrechos vínculos entre el magistrado del Tribunal Supremo Alexandre de Moraes y Vorcaro. La crisis institucional resultante en el seno del poderoso tribunal supremo impulsó un repunte del apoyo a Bolsonaro, quien lo aprovechó para renovar sus llamamientos a la destitución de Moraes, al tiempo que presentaba al juez que supervisó la condena de su padre como un aliado cercano de Lula. Esto ha desviado en gran medida la atención de las cuestiones económicas, a pesar de que los candidatos ofrecen visiones contrapuestas. Lula, quien desde hace tiempo ha defendido un enfoque de “gastar para crecer” centrado en estimular la demanda de los consumidores, ha supervisado una expansión constante y una tasa de desempleo cercana a mínimos históricos. Sin embargo, el crecimiento ha comenzado a ralentizarse en un contexto de tasas de interés elevadas, destinadas a situar la inflación en el objetivo del banco central, y los costos de financiación, que se mantienen en el 13,75%, han supuesto una carga tanto para las principales empresas brasileñas como para los consumidores. Por su parte, el déficit fiscal nominal ha aumentado hasta casi el 10% del producto interior bruto, mientras que la deuda pública se ha disparado por encima del 80%, lo que ha llevado a los inversores a analizar minuciosamente la campaña en busca de planes para sanear las cuentas de tal forma que resulte más fácil para los responsables políticos reducir los tipos de interés. Ver más: Mercados se preparan para fuertes fluctuaciones con independencia del resultado de las elecciones en Brasil Lula y sus asesores han alternado entre promesas de hacer frente a la deuda y cuestionar la necesidad de hacerlo: “Tenemos que acabar con esta tontería de generar superávits presupuestarios”, afirmó Lula en un acto celebrado en la recta final de la campaña. Bolsonaro, en un guiño a la política de austeridad impulsada por el líder libertario argentino Javier Milei, ha esgrimido unas tijeras para prometer un “gran recorte” en el gasto. Ha dado pocos detalles sobre sus planes, pero esto le ha convertido en la opción preferida de los inversores, que le consideran más propenso a llevar a cabo ajustes fiscales. Lula ha puesto en marcha una serie de medidas de estímulo este año con el fin de ayudar a los consumidores a acceder a créditos más baratos y aliviar las presiones de la deuda. En las últimas semanas de la campaña, ha aumentado las prestaciones sociales y ha presentado un plan para utilizar fondos públicos con el fin de comprar deudas morosas. Asimismo, ha prohibido los juegos de azar en línea, a los que ha culpado de sumir a los brasileños en el endeudamiento. Durante décadas, estas políticas funcionaron: Lula, un antiguo sindicalista, se convirtió en un icono mundial durante su primera presidencia, cuando guió a Brasil a través de un periodo de crecimiento explosivo y sacó de la pobreza a millones de personas. Volvió al poder hace cuatro años con la promesa de recuperar esa misma prosperidad. Sin embargo, aunque sigue siendo venerado por una amplia base de seguidores, le ha costado convencer a muchos votantes de que es capaz de satisfacer las demandas de un Brasil muy diferente al que gobernó anteriormente. Lula pareció reconocer esa realidad el domingo por la noche, al decir a sus seguidores en São Paulo que su partido y su campaña “necesitan replantearse cómo estamos haciendo las cosas”. -Con la colaboración de Augusta Saraiva, Martha Beck, Mariana Lumy, Catarina Bacci y Andrew Rosati. items.title: 消費者態度指数9月は前月比0.1ポイント低下、1年後の物価上昇見通し拡大
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Yoshifumi Takemoto

［東京　５日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Yoshifumi Takemoto

［東京　５日　ロイター］ - 内閣府が５日公表した９月の消費動向調査によると、足元の景況感を示す消費者態度指数は前月比０．１ポイント低下の３５．４となり、５カ月ぶりにマイナスに転じた。基調判断は「持ち直しの動きがみられる」で据え置いた。

消費者態度指数を構成する４指標のうち、「収入の増え方」と「雇用環境」は改善したものの、「暮らし向き」と「耐久消費財の買い時判断」の悪化幅が大きかった。

１年後の物価見通しは、上昇するとの回答比率が９０．６と前月比１．６ポイント拡大し、２カ月ぶりに９０％を超えた。１年後の物価が２％以上上昇するとの回答比率が前月比で増えた。コメ以外の食料品の価格上昇が影響した可能性は推察できると内閣府ではみている。

２０２２年のウクライナ侵略以降の物価上昇により、物価上昇見通しの上昇と「暮らし向き」判断などへの影響が推察されるが、内閣府では、９月の消費者態度指数への物価の影響は明確に判断できないとしている。

items.title: OKX joint venture files with SEC to launch tokenized trading platform
items.author: Gregor Hunter
items.creator: Gregor Hunter
items.summary: OKXICE, the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange , filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Sunday to launch a tokenized securities platform for around-the-clock trading of US stocks.
items.body:
OKXICE, the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE.N) , filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Sunday to launch a tokenized securities platform for around-the-clock trading of US stocks.
More than 60 listed companies will be available for around-the-clock trading throughout the week, according to the filing
"This is a landmark step toward a truly global, 24/7 Wall Street," said former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo, who is co-chair of OKXICE, in a post on the X social media platform
The SEC unveiled an [USN:L6N4590SA TEXT:"exemption"] last month allowing companies to offer trading in blockchain-based or "tokenized" stocks and other securities. The move came two days after comprehensive cryptocurrency legislation backed by US President Donald Trump [USN:L1N4570IP TEXT:"failed to advance"] in the Senate
Global exchanges including the NYSE, Nasdaq and the London Stock Exchange are preparing to launch round-the-clock trading in the coming months
Prediction markets' push into US stock trading has recently raised [USN:L6N44114G TEXT:"regulatory concerns"]

items.title: ロシアのドローンがキーウの橋に着弾、目撃者が撮影　メルツ独首相の訪問中
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
目撃者が撮影した映像には、ウクライナの首都キーウで4日、ロシアのドローンが北橋（ピブニチヌイ橋）に着弾する瞬間が映っている。ゼレンスキー大統領を支援する姿勢を示すためドイツのメルツ首相がキーウを訪問している最中の出来事だった。
キーウのクリチコ市長は交流サイト「テレグラム」で、ドローンは橋の路面に着弾したと説明。この橋は前日の3日にも攻撃を受けていた。
ロイターは、周辺の建物、道路の形状、橋、樹木が過去の記録映像や衛星写真と一致することから、現場を特定した。ロイターが撮影した攻撃後の映像でも、同じ場所の被害が確認されている。
ロシアは先週以降、キーウの橋への攻撃を続けており、ドニエプル川で東西に分かれた首都の両岸をつなぐ連絡路や、ウクライナ中部・東部を結ぶ物流路の寸断を狙っている。

items.title: NHL roundup: Mikael Granlund's OT goal hands Ducks win over Panthers
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Mikael Granlund's power-play goal with 46 seconds left in overtime gave the host Anaheim Ducks a 3-2 win over the Florida Panthers on Sunday night.
items.body:
Mikael Granlund's power-play goal with 46 seconds left in overtime gave the host Anaheim Ducks a 3-2 win over the Florida Panthers on Sunday night.
Granlund tipped in Carlsson's pass from the right corner for the winner, helping Anaheim win its first home game of the season.
Cutter Gauthier had two goals and an assist for the Ducks, who scored all three of their goals with the man advantage. Leo Carlsson contributed three assists and Lukas Dostal made 29 saves.
Carter Verhaeghe and Brad Marchand, making his season debut, got the goals for the Panthers, who have played into overtime in all three of their games this season. Jacob Markstrom stopped 18 shots.
Jets 3, Red Wings 2
Kyle Connor scored two power-play goals and added an assist to lift Winnipeg to a 3-2 victory over host Detroit.
Cole Perfetti scored the other goal and had two assists, while Josh Morrissey added two assists for the Jets, who went 3-for-4 on the power play. Stuart Skinner made 33 saves in Winnipeg's first victory of the season.
Viktor Arvidsson and Emmitt Finnie scored for the Red Wings, and John Gibson stopped 24 shots.
Rangers 4, Mammoth 2
Gabe Perreault scored the tiebreaking goal 3:15 into New York's three-goal third period during a win against visiting Utah.
Vladislav Gavrikov had a goal and an assist for the Rangers, who won their third straight. Igor Shesterkin made 28 saves in the victory and got the secondary assist on Tolvanen's empty-net goal with 1:15 remaining.
Nick Schmaltz scored Utah's sixth power-play goal through the team's first three games with 5:31 left in the second. Clayton Keller assisted on the goal, extending his regular-season point streak to 13 games.
Golden Knights 3, Canucks 2
Marc Gatcomb scored the go-ahead goal late in the second period and Adin Hill made 18 saves to lead Vegas past host Vancouver.
Mitch Marner and Victor Olofsson also scored goals for the Golden Knights, who improved to 22-4-3 all-time against the Canucks, including the last eight in a row. Hill, making his first start for Vegas since April 9 of last season, extended his personal win streak against Vancouver to five straight games.
Paul Cotter and Jonathan Lekkerimaki scored goals for Vancouver, which was playing the second game of a back-to-back that began with a 4-1 home victory over Calgary on Saturday. Kevin Lankinen stopped 25 of 28 shots for the Canucks.
Kraken 6, Flames 1
Mackie Samoskevich scored twice and Berkly Catton had a goal and an assist as Seattle convincingly won its home opener over Calgary.
Bobby McMann, Shane Wright and Jordan Eberle also scored, and Chandler Stephenson and Brandon Montour had two assists apiece for the Kraken, who rebounded from a 3-1 loss Saturday in Edmonton. Goaltender Joey Daccord made 32 saves.
Morgan Frost scored and Dustin Wolf stopped 21 of 27 shots for the Flames, who have been outscored 16-3 across their three losses to begin the season.
--Field Level Media

items.title: European EV sales hit record in 'pivotal' year for affordable cars, study shows
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Europe's uptake of electric vehicles is gaining momentum, with record sales so far this year driven by a slew of affordable models coming onto the market to bring carmakers in line with EU targets, according to a study.
items.body:
Europe's uptake of electric vehicles is gaining momentum, with record sales so far this year driven by a slew of affordable models coming onto the market to bring carmakers in line with EU targets, according to a study.
EV sales across the EU reached record volumes in 2026, with 1.64 million sold in the January-to-August period, up 45% year-on-year, Brussels-based environmental advocacy group Transport & Environment found in its EV progress report published on Monday.
EVs made up 22% of the market during this period, six points higher than the same period last year, according to the report.
T&E called 2026 "a pivotal year for EV availability", with model choice up 50% in a single year as carmakers expand their line-ups to meet EU emissions targets.
The report comes as carmakers like Volkswagen roll out a number of affordable EVs, such as the all-electric Polo, helping the German auto group to close its existing compliance gap and avoid fines.
European carmakers dominated the EV offering with nearly 60% of available models, adding 16 in the first half of 2026. Chinese carmakers held 21% and added 11 models.
The study also noted the impact of rising fuel prices linked to the Middle East conflict on drivers of combustion-engine cars. Diesel has risen the most, up 38% since the Iran war began, with a 50-litre tank now costing €30 ($34) more, it said.
($1 = €0.8890)

items.title: For freed Israeli hostages, every moment is now precious
items.author: Shir Torem, Hannah Confino
items.creator: Shir Torem, Hannah Confino
items.summary: Taken with their children or alone. Held for weeks, months or years. Confined in captors' homes or Hamas tunnels as war raged above them. Israeli former hostages seized on October 7 say they now cherish even the smallest moments of freedom.
items.body:
Aviva Siegel, 65, embraces her husband Keith Siegel, 67, both former hostages, as they watch the sunset from a field near their home in Kibbutz Gazit, northern Israel, August 6, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack was Israel's single deadliest day. The militants rampaged through villages, a music festival and army bases, killing 1,200 people and dragging 251 hostages back to Gaza.
They included civilians, soldiers, men, women, children and elderly people, Israelis and foreign nationals. Most were freed in return for Palestinian prisoners during ceasefires between Israel and Hamas, but dozens did not survive.

Emily Damari, 30

British-Israeli Emily Damari, 30, a former hostage, models during a photo shoot for her clothing brand which carries the slogan 'never lose yourself' and which, according to Emily, helps her manage her trauma by giving her purpose and a way to support her future and rehabilitation journey, in Tel Aviv, Israel, July 28, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

"Freedom has completely changed the way I see life," said Emily Damari, 30, who was abducted wounded from her home in Kibbutz Kfar Aza and released in January 2025.

Palestinian Hamas militants hand over Emily Damari to members of the International Committee of the Red Cross in Gaza City, January 19, 2025. REUTERS/Dawoud Abu Alkas/File Photo Emily Damari was abducted from her home in Kibbutz Kfar Aza after being shot in the hand and injured; she was held for 471 days before being released in January 2025. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Her ordeal taught her not to take anything for granted, she said. "One day in captivity feels like one week. You want to give up at every moment, but I did not," said Damari, who has recently married and launched a clothing line in Israel.
"Today, I open the fridge and I say thank you. I drink cold water and I say thank you. I am thankful for everything, big things and little things. Gratitude has become central to who I am," said Damari. "Being free, at home, surrounded by my family and my people is something I will never take for granted again."

Emily Damari looks in the mirror during a photo shoot for her clothing brand in Tel Aviv, Israel, July 28, 2026. "Freedom has completely changed the way I see life." REUTERS/Shir Torem

Emily Hand, 11

Emily Hand, 11, practices surfing through therapeutic surfing NGO HaGal Sheli, on Zikim beach in southern Israel, June 16, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Emily Hand was abducted from a friend's home in Kibbutz Beeri while staying there for a sleepover, along with her friend Hila Rotem and Hila's mother. REUTERS/Shir Torem Emily and and her friend Hila were taken to Gaza and held for 50 days before being released in November 2023. REUTERS/Shir Torem

I am trying to move on with my life. You can't just say 'it happened and it's over and that's it'. It happened but I am trying to detach from it. (When I surf) it's only me and the sea. I'm thinking of nothing else, only concentrating on the surf. Just me, the sea and the surfboard.
Emily Hand, 11, seized from Be'eri, released November 25 2023

Emily's father said that his daughter, who was 8 years old when she was taken hostage, could only speak in whispers following her release. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Eli Shararbi, 54

Eli Sharabi, 54, sits on a sofa during a tour of Shalva, a disability care and inclusion center in Jerusalem, July 30, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Eli Sharabi, 54, was seized from nearby Kibbutz Be'eri. His British-born wife Lianne and their two daughters Noiya, 16, and Yahel, 13, were slain by the attackers. His brother Yossi was taken hostage and killed in Gaza.
In February 2025, Sharabi was released, appearing emaciated and skeletally thin, from 491 days of captivity which he says included being held in a tunnel, hungry, shackled and beaten.

Eli Sharabi is released by Hamas militants after 491 days in captivity, in the central Gaza Strip, February 8, 2025. REUTERS/Hatem Khaled/File Photo Eli Sharabi laughs during a tour of Shalva, a disability care and inclusion center he is establishing in Jerusalem. REUTERS/Shir Torem

"I learned in captivity how precious every moment and every choice can be, and I carry that understanding with me now. I choose to look ahead, to keep going and to use the life I have in a meaningful way," said Sharabi.
Since his release he has helped establish the Shalva Sharabi Family Centre in the southern city of Ashkelon with the disability charity Shalva, to treat families coping with trauma and disabilities, in commemoration of his own family lost.
"I choose life. I choose to keep living fully, while carrying Lianne, Noiya, Yahel and Yossi with me in everything I do."
His wife and daughters believed deeply in caring for others, he said. "Their kindness and care for others will continue. Families will walk through these doors and receive help, care and hope in a place that carries their name. That gives me strength and makes me very proud," said Sharabi.

Eli Sharabi looks up at a banner depicting himself and his slain wife, Lianne, and daughters Noiya and Yahel at Shalva, the disability care and inclusion center he is establishing in Jerusalem, July 30, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Doron Steinbrecher, 32

Doron Steinbrecher, 32, watches the sunset with her beloved dog, Pal, on a beach in Shefayim, Israel, August 12, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Hamas militants hand over Doron Steinbrecher, held in captivity for 471 days, to members of the International Committee of the Red Cross in Gaza City, January 19, 2025. REUTERS/via Reuters TV/File Photo Doron Steinbrecher was abducted from her home in Kibbutz Kfar Aza after calling her parents to tell them she was scared and that gunmen had arrived at her building; she was taken hostage to Gaza and held for 471 days before being released in January 2025. REUTERS/Shir Torem

What gives me strength today are my friends, family, and even my dog. The people who fought for me to be here and want to see me heal, be happy, and fulfill myself. Every day is a reminder of how nothing can be taken for granted and that I received my life as a gift, so I have to make the most of it and do everything that makes me feel good.
Doron Steinbrecher, 33, seized from Kfar Aza, released January 2025

Doron Steinbrecher, 32, with her beloved dog, Pal, on a beach in Shefayim, Israel, August 12, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Hagar Brodutch, 43

Hagar Brodutch, 43, adds the final touches to a tart during a class at a culinary school where she is learning French pastry, in Tel Aviv, Israel, September 16, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Hagar Brodutch was seized from Kfar Aza with her three children and her neighbours' daughter who fled to their house after her parents were killed. They were freed in a brief truce in November 2023.
Life after captivity, she said, can be far more complicated than sometimes portrayed.
"The daily struggle is immense, especially for children. I believe it will take many more years before captivity becomes just a shadow that walks alongside us, rather than something that defines who we are," said Brodutch.
Recently, Brodutch, 43, has begun taking classes in pastry baking, for which she has long had a passion.
"This is about much more than learning how to bake. It is about finding a new path, creating something with my own hands, and slowly building a future," she said.
"During my time in Hamas captivity, I began to understand that if I were released, returning to my previous life and working in management might no longer be possible," said Brodutch.
"I chose pastry as a form of therapy, but also as a way to create something new for myself, with the hope that one day it could become my profession," she said.

Hagar was abducted from her home in Kibbutz Kfar Aza along with her three children, and their three-year-old neighbour; all five were taken hostage to Gaza and held for 51 days before being released in November 2023. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Agam Berger, 22

Agam Berger, 22, practices the violin ahead of performances at two memorial ceremonies for the third anniversary of October 7 at her home in Holon, Israel, September 17, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

What gives me strength is my family, the people of Israel, to be involved in meaningful activity and to give others the strength of hope.
Agam Berger, 22, abducted from her military base near the Gaza border, released January 2025

Hamas militants release Israeli soldier Agam Berger in Gaza, January 30, 2025. REUTERS/Dawoud Abu Alkas/File Photo Agam Berger was abducted from the Nahal Oz military base in southern Israel, where she was serving as a surveillance soldier, and taken hostage to Gaza, where she was held for 482 days before being released in January 2025. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Aviva and Keith Siegel, 62 and 65

Aviva Siegel, 65, holds her husband Keith Siegel, 67, both former hostages, as they watch the sunset from a field near their home in Kibbutz Gazit, northern Israel, August 6, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Kfar Aza was one of the hardest-hit communities in Hamas' attack. Aviva Siegel, 62, was kidnapped with her husband Keith, 65. She was released in November 2023, but Keith was held until February 2025.

Aviva Siegel reacts following her release, in Ofakim, Israel, November 26, 2023. REUTERS/Amir Cohen/File Photo Aviva was released after 51 days, while Keith remained in captivity for 484 days before being released in February 2025. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Aviva joined the hostage release campaign movement in Israel while her husband was still being held. Their reunion and her children and grandchildren, and even strangers she meets, give her strength every day, she says.
"I feel that I’m not alone and that there's so much love in this world and we need to keep it with both our hands," she said. "I feel very, very lucky to be alive."

Aviva Siegel, 65, and her husband Keith Siegel, 67, both former hostages, during a walk at sunset with two of their grandchildren near their home in Kibbutz Gazit, northern Israel, August 6, 2026. Aviva says her strength comes from having Keith by her side and being with her children and grandchildren. REUTERS/Shir Torem
