items.title: Lab worker's death from 'unknown infection' sparks plague fears in Russia, hundreds quarantined
items.summary: Russian authorities are investigating a lab worker's death from unidentified pneumonia at a Siberian research facility. While officials report a stable public health situation, the incident has ...
items.body:
Lab worker's death from 'unknown infection' sparks plague fears in Russia, hundreds quarantined Russian authorities are investigating a lab worker's death from unidentified pneumonia at a Siberian research facility. While officials report a stable public health situation, the incident has sparked fears of pneumonic plague and prompted precautionary measures, including close medical monitoring of contacts.
ANI | Updated: 05-10-2026 09:02 IST | Created: 05-10-2026 09:02 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Russia

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Authorities in Russia are responding to an alleged research facility mishap in Siberia following the fatality of a laboratory technician who suffered from an affliction categorised as pneumonia of “unknown” origin, according to CNN. The occurrence unfolded at the Anti-Plague Research Institute situated in Shelekhov near Irkutsk, based on reports from Russian state-run news outlet TASS.
Uncertainty persists regarding the specific pathogen involved, as Rospotrebnadzor, Russia’s federal body responsible for infectious disease oversight, stated that the staff member received a diagnosis of “pneumonia of unknown aetiology”, indicating an unidentified origin. According to CNN, Rospotrebnadzor maintained that “the sanitary and epidemiological situation in the Irkutsk region, the cities of Irkutsk and Shelekhov is stable”.
The agency added that it implemented specialised protocols “in connection with the case of an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute”. Despite official reassurances, the fatality has sparked anxieties surrounding a potential instance of pneumonic plague.
Alexei Tsydenov, leader of the adjacent republic of Buryatia, noted that the deceased 28-year-old female worker perished “possibly from the plague”, while emphasising to CNN that “there are no plague outbreaks” within Buryatia. Following an emergency gathering of the local anti-epidemic council alongside Russia’s primary state medical officer, Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev appealed for public composure on Friday.
As reported by CNN, Kobzev explained that the session connected to a “suspected case of a particularly dangerous infection affecting a resident of the region”. Additional safety steps have similarly been established across the vicinity of Shelekhov.
An industrial aluminium facility situated close to the research centre directed personnel to utilise face coverings. Artem Fominikh, who heads the Irkutsk Aluminium Plant, advised individuals to stay tranquil amidst circulating speculation, stating via CNN that “there are many rumours and conflicting reports circulating”.
“All identified close contacts are under medical supervision. At present, they show no signs of the disease, and their laboratory test results are negative,” Fominikh remarked, according to CNN. CNN additionally noted that unverified accounts from the independent local publication Liudi Baikala suggested nearly 200 individuals faced monitoring procedures at the Shelekhov medical facility where the lab worker received treatment.
The publication further indicated that isolation protocols were enacted at a minimum of one maternity facility inside the municipality. Such lockdown claims have heightened apprehension about the event, even as Russian officials insist the public health climate stays steady.
Gennady Onishchenko, previously leading Rospotrebnadzor, expressed his assessment that the Siberian pathogen was “most likely not the plague”, asserting further that even if the plague were verified, “there will be no spread of this disease”. Pneumonic plague represents one of three variants of plague triggered by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. Contrary to alternative strains usually transmitted via interaction with tainted fleas, fauna, or contaminated tissues, pneumonic plague targets the respiratory system and is capable of transmitting between humans via airborne respiratory droplets, drawing on details referenced by CNN.
Individuals suffering from pneumonic plague commonly experience elevated temperatures, cranial discomfort, and fatigue, preceding fast-onset pneumonia, breathing difficulties, thoracic discomfort, coughing fits, and occasionally blood-tinged or fluid-like secretions, per documentation from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. (ANI)

items.body:
TSMC in talks with Musk over potential role in Texas Terafab, discussions at early stage Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) is in talks over a potential role in Elon Musk’s planned Terafab foundry in Texas, with the discussions still at an early stage, according to a report by Taiwan Plus.
ANI | Updated: 05-10-2026 08:55 IST | Created: 05-10-2026 08:55 IST

The logo of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is displayed at its fabrication plant in Kaohsiung, Taiwan. (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) is in talks over a potential role in Elon Musk’s planned Terafab foundry in Texas, with the discussions still at an early stage, according to a news report by Taiwan Plus. TSMC Chairman and CEO CC Wei said the timeline for building and scaling a new wafer fabrication plant could be a key consideration as the companies discuss the project.
Wei said a new wafer fabrication plant would take about two to three years to build, while expanding its production capacity could require another one to two years, calling it a “fundamental” of the foundry industry, Taiwan Plus reported. The report said one option under discussion would have TSMC own and operate the Texas plant, while SpaceX would invest in the project and purchase chips produced at the facility. Another option would give SpaceX a majority stake in the plant.
Musk has confirmed the discussions with TSMC on X, saying the talks are still at an early stage, Taiwan Plus reported. The potential Texas project comes as TSMC continues to expand its manufacturing presence in the United States. Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs had approved applications for TSMC to invest USD 44 billion in the United States since December 2020, according to an earlier Focus Taiwan report.
TSMC announced in March 2025 that it planned an additional USD 100 billion investment in Arizona, on top of an earlier USD 65 billion plan, taking its overall planned investment in the state to USD 165 billion. The expanded Arizona plan included increasing the number of planned advanced wafer fabrication facilities from three to six, along with two advanced integrated circuit assembly units and a dedicated research facility, according to Focus Taiwan.
For the proposed Texas Terafab, the ownership structure and TSMC’s eventual role remain under discussion. With the talks still at an early stage, the proposed operating and investment arrangements have yet to be finalised. (ANI)

items.title: France's Schneider Electric confirms $22.6 billion deal to buy US software firm PTC
items.author: Sabrina Valle
items.creator: Sabrina Valle
items.summary: France's Schneider Electric said on Monday it had agreed to buy PTC in an all-cash deal valuing the US software company's equity at around $22.6 billion, confirming reports from Sunday.
items.body:
France's Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) said on Monday it had agreed to buy PTC (PTC.O) in an all-cash deal valuing the US software company's equity at around $22.6 billion, confirming reports from Sunday.
The $205-per-share offer implies an enterprise value of $23.7 billion for Boston-based PTC and represents a 42.3% premium to its last closing share price.
The deal will be financed through a combination of equity and new debt issuance and is expected to be closed in the third quarter of 2027.
The acquisition would deepen the French engineering company's push into software acquisitions, having agreed to buy [USN:L6N432112 TEXT:"Cognite Holding"], a privately held provider of AI software and industrial data, in June.
Schneider, once known primarily for industrial components like fuses and circuit breakers, now builds the backbone of data centres, supplying everything from cooling units and server racks to critical power distribution equipment.
The booming demand for data centres, particularly from the United States, is driving [USN:L6N41D0F0 TEXT:"Schneider's earnings"], offering a growing source of revenue helping offset weakness in some traditional electrical-equipment markets.
PTC, which provides software solutions for designing, manufacturing and servicing products across multiple sectors, has also [USN:L4N43V2I2 TEXT:"benefited"] from growing demand for its AI-powered tools.
In July, Schneider Electric lifted its [USN:L4N43V2I2 TEXT:"annual revenue forecast"] after reporting record first-half results, betting on strong demand for its core industrial software and artificial intelligence-powered tools.

Oct 4 : SpaceX CEO Elon Musk posted on Sunday that he would rename the company's AI unit to SpaceXSI, following US President Donald Trump's push to use the term "super intelligence" instead of "artificial intelligence."
"Yes, we will make that change," he replied to a user on X asking him about the possibility of renaming SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI. 
Here are a few more details: 
• At the time of publication, SpaceXAI's X account had not been changed.

• Musk did not provide any additional information regarding the name change, nor did he give a potential timeline for when the change would occur.
• SpaceXAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding the change.
• In a speech last month to the UN General Assembly, Trump said: "From this point forward, all of United States documents, and hopefully the world's will be changed to use the much more accurate term 'super' as opposed to artificial. So it's super intelligence."

items.title: 48 Hours in the Singapore With No Smartphone

(Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Yemeni government launches offensive to seize all areas from Iran-backed Houthis
items.author: Mohammed Ghobari, Timour Azhari, Eman Abouhassira
items.creator: Mohammed Ghobari, Timour Azhari, Eman Abouhassira
items.summary: Despite the preparations for a counteroffensive, the Houthis have maintained the initiative on the ground, weeks after seizing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in a lightning offensive that saw government forces collapse.
items.body:
Yemen’s Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government said on Sunday it was launching a major military campaign to recapture all areas of the country controlled by the Iran-backed Houthis .
The government’s armed forces would press the offensive “until the country is liberated from the grip of the terrorist militia,” Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address. A military spokesman later called on the Houthis to lay down their weapons.
The Houthis, known formally as Ansar Allah, have held Yemen’s capital Sanaa and vast parts of the northwest, where most of the population live, since 2014. They have so far withstood a series of attacks over the years by Saudi Arabia, the UAE and their Western allies, and have updated their weaponry with the help of Iran.
The movement launched a surprise offensive last month which captured the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait and some 150 km (90 miles) of coast on the Red Sea in a matter of weeks, giving the Houthis new leverage over the international shipping route.
That advance also opened a new front in the wider US-Israeli war launched in February against Iran, to which Tehran’s responses included choking oil shipping through the Strait of Hormuz , to the other side of the Arabian Peninsula.
HOUTHIS SAY THEY STRUCK SAUDI ARABIA As the Yemeni government, known as the Presidential Leadership Council, made its announcement, the Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia.
They claimed the attacks caused major fires and were in response to what they said were 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen in the past 12 hours.
There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.
Alimi said the decision to launch the counteroffensive came after all chances of de-escalating the conflict had been exhausted.
He thanked Saudi Arabia for its support and called on Yemen's regional allies and international partners to support PLC forces and institutions.
Regional and western officials had told Reuters earlier this week that Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies were planning to [USN:L8N45M1W0 TEXT:"launch an assault"] on the Houthis, with the Saudis leading aerial combat and Yemeni forces fighting on the ground.
NEW FRONT IN MIDEAST WAR The US is already providing intelligence to support Riyadh's operations in Yemen, while some regional and European nations are providing mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom, six people with knowledge of the Saudi preparations told Reuters.
The United States’ war on Iran has decimated a layer of Iranian military and political leadership, but has also entangled Washington in a new engagement in the Middle East and depleted crucial military hardware.
Yemen has been mired in conflict for years, with an array of local armed groups and factions backed by competing regional and international actors.
After a popular uprising that was part of the Arab Spring movements in 2011, the Houthis, an armed group of Zaidi Shi’ite Muslims, captured Sanaa.
The Saudi-backed PLC, which is also recognised by the United Nations, has since the Houthi takeover controlled the south and east of the country, based in the former South Yemen capital of Aden.
Saudi Arabia entered Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition in support of the PLC, but failed to defeat the Houthis.
A truce agreed between the warring parties in 2022 largely held until this year, when the Houthis launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure in a spillover from the Iran war.
HOUTHIS ON FRONT FOOT The Houthis have maintained the initiative on the ground since seizing control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in their lightning offensive last month that saw government forces collapse.
Bab el-Mandeb is the southern exit passage of the Red Sea, a key shipping route between the Mediterranean and Asia that has assumed even more importance this year as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.
In the last 48 hours, the Houthis have also made gains against government and local forces on strategic hilltops near Yemen's Taiz, military sources said, advancing on the last road between the city and Aden on the southern coast.
Houthi control over the Taiz-Aden road would lead to an effective siege of the city, Yemen's third-largest, inhabited by hundreds of thousands of civilians and where thousands of government forces are also stationed.
The city is important not just for its strategic location; Alimi is from the region, and a siege of Taiz would amplify an already-dire humanitarian situation in the country.
Three in four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry from the impact of the surge in fighting, which has displaced tens of thousands of people and disrupted supplies to millions, the World Food Programme said last week.

items.title: Saudi Arabia to cancel Joy Awards, its answer to the Grammys, amid budget cuts, sources say
items.author: Timour Azhari
items.creator: Timour Azhari
items.summary: Saudi Arabia is set to cancel next year's Joy Awards, its star-studded answer to the Oscars or the Grammys, as financial strain and the Iran war hit the country's nascent entertainment sector, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia is set to cancel next year's Joy Awards, its star-studded answer to the Oscars or the Grammys, as financial strain and the Iran war hit the country's nascent entertainment sector, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
Held in January, the event has become the crown jewel of Riyadh's annual events calendar, drawing performers including Katy Perry and Robbie Williams this year and handing out awards in music as well as other areas of entertainment and sport.
It is the latest high-profile entertainment event to face cancellation or postponement as Riyadh reprioritizes spending and cuts culture and entertainment budgets.
A spokesperson for the General Entertainment Authority, which organizes the Joy Awards along with Saudi media conglomerate MBC Group, did not respond to a request for comment. MBC Group and the Saudi government's media office also did not respond to requests for comment.
Industry sources say budget cuts were already felt before the Iran war, which has undermined Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's efforts to turn the kingdom into a destination for tourism and global events under his ambitious Vision 2030 plan.
Flagship projects scaled back or indefinitely postponed over the last year or so include the 100-mile (161 km) steel and glass tower The Line at megacity NEOM, and a $50 billion steel and metal [USN:L1N3YR0WK TEXT:"cube"] in Riyadh. The government has also withdrawn funding from ventures such as LIV Golf, after spending over $5 billion on the startup, and is now quietly shelving plans to [USN:L6N45E0H2 TEXT:"build"] the NEOM Stadium, one of the main projects for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said.
"The war and its wider ripple effects are inevitably prompting Gulf states to reassess spending priorities," said Mazen Hayek, a Dubai-based media consultant.
"It's not simply a question of whether governments have the financial capacity to fund such initiatives. Some of these events were also conceived as instruments of international visibility, soft power and influence. In the current environment, however, governments may be weighing those objectives against other national priorities," he said.
FILM FESTIVAL, DESERT RAVE ALSO CANCELLED Last month, the Red Sea Film Festival was postponed until 2027, with organizers citing logistical constraints and other factors. Uncertainty over the Iran war has also made it difficult to book international stars for such events, the industry sources said.
The Red Sea Film Festival was launched in 2021 as part of an effort to develop local cinema after Saudi Arabia lifted a decades-long ban on cinemas.
Last month, organizers also called off Soundstorm, a city-sized rave in the desert due to be held in December that welcomes hundreds of thousands of partygoers and was headlined by Cardi B last year. Organizers said it would return next year, giving no reason for the cancellation.
Soundstorm, also known as MDLBEAST, began in 2019 as new events were staged amid rapid social change under the crown prince, widely known as MbS, whose reforms sought to rein in the power of religious conservatives.
With gender-mixing, dancing and displays of queer culture, the festival often drew the ire of religious conservatives and stunned even some of those who support other aspects of the kingdom's social opening.
Events aimed at driving investment into the kingdom, such as the flagship Future Investment Initiative (FII) taking place at the end of this month, remain scheduled as planned, according to organizers.
"Events that are important for the Saudi economy and showing its place in the world are still being prioritised; what isn't is anything that is singing and dancing and having a good time," a person working in the Saudi events industry said.

items.title: Australia probes flydubai co-pilot's links to the country, police say
items.author: Praveen Menon, Alexander Cornwell
items.creator: Praveen Menon, Alexander Cornwell
items.summary: The co-pilot, identified as an Omani, studied at a university in Melbourne, sources said.
items.body:
A multi-agency Australian counterterrorism unit is investigating links to Australia of the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073, who stabbed his captain and then [USN:L1N45P01E TEXT:"attempted to hijack"] the plane, a police spokesperson said on Sunday.
The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team – which comprises federal police, Victorian state police and the ASIO intelligence agency – was "investigating the man's links to Australia," the Australian Federal Police spokesperson said.
Two sources briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne, the capital of the Australian state of Victoria, without identifying which one. A third source said he studied at RMIT University in Melbourne around a decade ago.
In a brief statement on Monday, RMIT confirmed that the co-pilot had been enrolled at the university but he did not successfully complete an engineering qualification. RMIT did not name the co-pilot or say when he studied there.
The co-pilot of the [USN:L1N45P02M TEXT:"flydubai flight FZ1073"], which was bound for Israel from Dubai on Wednesday, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a "[USN:S8N43T02Z TEXT:"terrorist attack"]".
Flight FZ1073 would have felt like a [USN:L4N45Q00M TEXT:""vertical roller coaster""], when it plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters.
CO-PILOT IN CUSTODY IN UAE Two sources have said the co-pilot is an Omani national named Hamam Al-Hammami. Israeli officials have not named the co-pilot but said that he is from Oman. UAE authorities and flydubai have not publicly disclosed the co-pilot's identity.
Reuters could not independently reach Al-Hammami, who is in UAE custody, for comment. The UAE has not announced any formal charges against him and it is not known if he has appointed legal counsel. Oman has not commented on the incident.
Disaster on board flight FZ1073 was averted after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an attempt to crash the plane carrying more than 170 passengers and crew. The UAE public prosecutor has said the co-pilot had attempted to take control of the plane.
RADICAL MOSQUES AND EXTREMIST WEBSITES Most of the passengers on board were Israeli nationals.
A reserve flydubai pilot travelling on the flight took control of the aircraft and landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where the co-pilot was detained by Saudi authorities and later transferred to the UAE on Thursday.
The Financial Times reported on Sunday that Al-Hamami had allegedly visited what it described as radical mosques and extremist websites while in Australia, citing two people familiar with the investigation. Australian intelligence services held a file on the individual, according to the Financial Times.
Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. The government of Australia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside normal business hours.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the co-pilot had undergone radical [USN:L6N45N0GW TEXT:"Islamist indoctrination"] and was clearly suicidal, although he has not said when or where that indoctrination allegedly occurred.
On Sunday he instructed the National Security Council to appoint an examiner to "conduct a thorough review of all security aspects regarding foreign civil aviation to Israel".
Israel does not have official diplomatic relations with Oman, and Netanyahu has also said pilots from such countries were not permitted to operate flights to Israel. It is not clear how the co-pilot came to be assigned to the flight to Tel Aviv.

items.title: Bolsonaro will face Lula in runoff in Brazil's presidential vote
items.author: Luciana Magalhaes, Lisandra Paraguassu, Ricardo Brito, Brendan O'Boyle
items.creator: Luciana Magalhaes, Lisandra Paraguassu, Ricardo Brito, Brendan O'Boyle
items.summary: Right-wing Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a runoff of the presidential election later this month, after he exceeded expectations in Sunday's first-round vote with a slight lead over the incumbent.
items.body:
Right-wing Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a runoff of the presidential election later this month, after he exceeded expectations in Sunday's first-round vote with a slight lead over the incumbent.
The election, which centered around the [USN:L6N459162 TEXT:"cost of living"], corruption and insecurity in Brazilians' daily lives, follows a string of wins across Latin America by right-wing parties aligned with US President Donald Trump.
Bolsonaro's stronger-than-expected performance, at 47% of votes versus Lula's 45%, is expected to buoy his campaign and may bolster Brazil's currency and stock market, which have risen on the prospects of the business-friendly challenger. Private surveys in the run-up to the election had forecast Lula leading the first-round vote by around 3 percentage points.
"Brazil wants change and I am very happy with the results," Bolsonaro told reporters in Brasilia after nearly all tallies were reported, heralding "the end of the era of (Lula's) Workers' Party."
The senator, son of [USN:L1N45F0NC TEXT:"right-wing former President"] Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year [USN:S0N3UJ08N TEXT:"sentence"] for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election, now heads to an October 25 showdown with the [USN:L1N45G04J TEXT:"leftist Lula"].
Addressing a crowd at a hotel in Sao Paulo, Lula said he had been convinced he would win the election in the first round.
"Starting tomorrow, we begin a new campaign," he said, promising to show voters what he had accomplished as president.
Despite growing worries over Brazil's public finances and sluggish economic growth, the campaign offered [USN:L1N4580UE TEXT:"meager policy debate"], as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates.
SURPRISE SHOWING "The pollsters missed badly," said Robert Muggah, cofounder of think-tank Igarape Institute. "Expect the runoff polls, which show a dead heat, to understate Bolsonaro as well."
Early on Sunday, Bolsonaro told journalists in Rio de Janeiro he was counting on "a protest vote from people who would otherwise vote for another candidate but are opposed to Lula."
Thaise Lima, a 41-year-old lawyer on her way to vote in Sao Paulo, said her main goal was to get Lula's Workers' Party out of office.
"I don't think Flavio is the best candidate, but I might decide to vote for him in the next few minutes," she said, adding that she wished psychiatrist and author Augusto Cury were a more viable candidate.
Fernando Tempel, 49, a management consultant, told Reuters he was voting for Bolsonaro despite initially planning to vote for Romeu Zema, the former governor of Minas Gerais state.
"The protest vote foreshadows what is to come in the runoff," said political analyst Rafael Favetti. "While this should benefit Flavio Bolsonaro now, his growth potential in the second round drops precisely because that support has already been front-loaded."
ECONOMIC HEADWINDS Despite Brazil's [USN:L1N44111S TEXT:"falling inequality"] and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over voters grappling with the high cost of living, heavy household debt and the threat of crime and more pervasive gang activity.
Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns, while Lula moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families.
Rising spending and public debt above 82% of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil's next president will need to address. The government lowered its [USN:L1N45E0QC TEXT:"economic growth forecasts"] for this year and next to 2.0% and 2.3%, respectively.
"I voted for Brazil to start growing again," said Marciano de Souza e Silva, a 52-year-old public servant in Brasilia who voted for Flavio.
OVERSHADOWED DEBATE Scandals and fears of foreign interference ahead of the vote largely overshadowed policy debates during the campaign.
Controversy surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master engulfed much of Brazil's political class after Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier this year and accused of a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme, which he denies.
A federal police investigation has looked into the banker's ties to figures across Brazil's political elite, including Bolsonaro, who is being [USN:L1N4530BQ TEXT:"investigated for "][USN:L1N4530BQ TEXT:"suspected money "][USN:L1N4530BQ TEXT:"laundering"] that police have tied to the case. Bolsonaro has denied wrongdoing.
Throughout the campaign, Lula's allies have warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognize election results if he wins, pointing to an aborted effort to [USN:L6N43R03C TEXT:"send US officials to Brazil"].
Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, though he hosted Senator Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly.
Reuters reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials briefed a French and German delegation on [USN:L1N45E08V TEXT:"alleged US and Russian interference"] before the election. The US has rejected claims of interference in Brazil's affairs.
On Sunday afternoon, Brazil's electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques said the election was running smoothly.

items.title: Like a 'vertical roller coaster': Simulating flight FZ1073's sudden plunge
items.author: Ben Makori
items.creator: Ben Makori
items.summary: A prolonged high-speed dive can place extreme strain on an airframe, an expert says.
items.body:
Flydubai's [USN:S8N44D013 TEXT:"flight FZ1073"], which plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, would have felt like a "vertical roller coaster", according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters.
The steep fall, after an attack on the captain by the co-pilot during a flight on Wednesday, would have put huge strain on the Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft - as well as the passengers and crew, said Alberto Paduanelli, owner of ALPA Simulation in Sherfield on Loddon, southern England.
The co-pilot of the flydubai jet, which was bound for Israel from Dubai, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a "[USN:L1N45P01E TEXT:"terrorist attack"]".
The co-pilot was identified as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, two sources with knowledge of the investigation told Reuters. UAE authorities did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation of his identity. Reuters could not independently reach al-Hammami for comment.
Flydubai says the circumstances surrounding the incident are still under investigation and it cannot comment further. Oman has yet to comment on the incident.
"A plunge of 16,000 feet (4,877 metres) over 30 seconds will feel like you are over on a very, very vertical roller coaster," Paduanelli said, sitting at the controls of the simulator cockpit.
"The difference is that on the roller coaster, you know what's happening," he said, adding that with a sudden drop "you feel the negative g-force on your body".
For passengers who are not strapped in, "Your body will literally lift from the seat", he said.
Using a simulator to recreate the incident, Paduanelli said the aircraft's autopilot disconnected before the plunge began, causing the jet to accelerate rapidly.
US President Donald Trump has praised the Boeing jet for withstanding the severe forces put on it during the incident. The plane was levelled out after passengers overpowered the co-pilot, before a reserve crew of pilots onboard landed the plane.
"It was an amazing show of precise and powerful structural planning and design," Trump posted on Truth Social, adding that the 737 Max "was able to withstand G Forces and Strain far beyond what it was designed and expected to do".
Boeing did not respond to a request for comment.
Aircraft are designed and tested to withstand substantial aerodynamic loads, but Paduanelli said a prolonged high-speed dive can place extreme strain on an airframe.
"This was nothing but a miracle that nothing was hurt apart from the captain, unfortunately, and that two pilots were onboard," Paduanelli said.
Details about al-Hammami's past have trickled out.
Royal Air Maroc told Reuters he did a three-month training with the airline in 2025 but his application to work there afterwards was rejected. Buckinghamshire New University in Britain said he did a distance-learning course in aviation management with the institution, but no pilot training.
An Australian Federal Police spokesperson said on Sunday that authorities there were investigating al-Hammami's "links to Australia". A source briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne.

items.title: Saudi Arabia quietly shelving NEOM Stadium, one of 2034 World Cup venues
items.author: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
items.creator: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
items.summary: It was meant to be one of the most ambitious venues for the 2034 FIFA World Cup.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia is quietly shelving plans to build one of its most ambitious stadiums for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said, after delays and downscaling of the futuristic development housing it.
The NEOM Stadium was billed as an elevated arena in a glitzy 100-mile (160-km) steel and glass structure known as The Line, in turn part of the broader development known as NEOM.
NEOM was introduced about a decade ago as a centrepiece of de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's Vision 2030, an ambitious plan to diversify the economy and cut reliance on oil.
Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of NEOM's owner the Public Investment Fund, confirmed in April that The Line was [USN:S8N40J01E TEXT:"no longer a priority"], and said it was not vital before 2030, the original delivery target for its first phase. He denied any projects had been cancelled.
However, according to two sources, plans to build the NEOM Stadium have now been shelved indefinitely.
NEOM and the Saudi government media office did not reply to requests for comment, while Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Sports redirected questions to the World Cup 2034 Hosting Higher Authority.
The Authority said "substantial delivery" of construction milestones for the event was already taking place, but did not address questions around the NEOM Stadium and costs. It shared images of some of the other stadiums under construction.
RIYADH DEVELOPING 15 VENUES FOR 2034 WORLD CUP The 2034 World Cup is seen as a marquee event for Saudi Arabia, which under the Vision 2030 programme has invested heavily in sports via wealth fund PIF. The tournament will be the first time a single nation hosts the expanded 48-team format.
Riyadh is working to build or renovate 15 venues across five cities, as well as dozens of training facilities.
MEED Projects, a Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform whose team of analysts tracks tenders and projects in the region, puts the total value of the projects at $22.7 billion in data shared with Reuters.
According to MEED, NEOM's stadium is expected to cost $2.5 billion. It lists the projected 46,000-seat stadium in its data as "on hold".
The stadium has no listed completion date, according to the data, which describes the remaining stadiums and facilities as in various stages of development, with completion expected between 2026 and 2033.
Saudi Arabia is under increasing pressure from the Iran war, which has led to heavy disruptions to energy shipments and damage to critical infrastructure, with the kingdom facing attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis.
Last week, the Ministry of Finance said it [USN:L1N45M0WE TEXT:"expected"] a fiscal deficit this year wider than previously projected and a real GDP contraction of 3.6% following a drop in oil activities.
PIVOT FROM GIGA-PROJECTS The geographic distribution of the stadiums adds to the challenge of delivering the projects, a third source said. That could further be compounded by some projects set to host stadiums being delayed or downsized, such as The Line or Riyadh's New Murabba development, the source added.
In January Reuters [USN:L1N3YR0WK TEXT:"reported"] that Saudi Arabia has suspended construction of The Mukaab, a colossal cube-shaped skyscraper at the centre of the New Murabba.
Reuters also reported last year that the PIF was pivoting from its focus on costly giga-projects to endeavours with more immediate financial returns, a strategy [USN:L1N40Y0DC TEXT:"later articulated"] by Saudi officials.
Still, other projects for the World Cup are progressing. The [USN:L6N43I0ZY TEXT:"Aramco Stadium"] in the eastern city of Al Khobar is set to be completed by the end of this year and host its first game in January, for which tickets are on sale.
Work on other planned stadiums is going ahead, a fourth source said.

items.title: Revolut's rise to become Europe's $115 billion big bank rival
items.author: Lawrence White, Elizabeth Howcroft
items.creator: Lawrence White, Elizabeth Howcroft
items.summary: Revolut has become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, though it faces hurdles.
items.body:
Revolut has risen to become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, having grown rapidly since it was launched just over a decade ago as a fintech promising cheaper forex fees.
Yet Revolut faces many hurdles itself, with the amount of revenue it extracts per customer a fraction of its established competitors and a small lending business by industry standards.
A spokesperson for Revolut said in an email that the London-based company has a "diversified business model", earning its revenue from various products and services rather than lending.
"That means our growth depends on building things customers value, rather than on interest rates," the spokesperson said.
Here's Revolut's rise, in five charts:
GOING FOR GLOBAL CEO Nik Storonsky has stressed he wants Revolut to be truly global, expanding into markets [USN:L4N44E0AO TEXT:"from Mexico to Australia"].
The company has announced several new licences in recent weeks, as it aims to become one of only a handful of banks with retail operations spanning so much of the globe.
Meanwhile, some traditional lenders seen as global, including HSBC (HSBA.L) , are reducing their retail footprint.
Valued at $115 billion privately, Revolut is now worth more than Britain's Barclays (BARC.L) and France's Societe Generale (SOGN.PA) as investors bet on its tech platform winning over more customers globally.
Revolut's 2025 pretax profit was £1.7 billion ($2.2 billion), a fraction of Barclays' £9 billion, but growing fast.
Paulo Macedo, CEO of Portugal's biggest bank, Caixa Geral de Depósitos, said in June that 2025 was the last year in which the 150-year-old bank would record higher profit than Revolut.
"When you go to Europe the bank CEOs there are talking about Revolut as their most important threat because of their aggressive marketing and growth," said Cihan Duran, director at S&P Global Ratings.
MARRED BY SETBACKS In the US, where Revolut has a provisional license, it will face tougher competition, investors said.
"The US could be potentially the biggest growth for Revolut. But at the same time, the US is the most competitive market," said Konstantin Sidorov, CEO of the London Technology Club, which invested in Revolut when it was valued at just $5.5 billion.
There have been setbacks, including a fine in Lithuania for failing to prevent money laundering. Revolut said an investigation had not identified any confirmed instances of money laundering, adding that it had signed a settlement with the central bank and taken steps to resolve shortcomings.
And in September, Revolut accidentally sent customer data to hackers posing as government investigators. The company said its systems and customer funds were unaffected and it had contacted the "limited number of impacted individuals" to give support.
In 2024 and 2025, Revolut was the most-complained-about bank in Britain in fraud cases whereby customers are tricked into sending cash to scammers, Ombudsman data compiled by consumer advocacy firm Which? showed.
Revolut has previously said in response it takes fraud very seriously and has robust customer protections in place.
CUSTOMERS HAVE SURGED A striking measure of its growth is customer numbers.
In Ireland, for example, Revolut said that 80% of the adult population has a Revolut account.
Revolut's website shows it has 80 million customers, against 84 million for JPMorgan (JPM.N) and 41 million for HSBC.
REVENUE-PER-CUSTOMER IS LOW Revolut makes far less from each of its customers than traditional banks, a Reuters analysis of its figures shows. Average deposit balances are also much lower.
Lower per-customer revenue is in part because Revolut lends much less than traditional banks, instead relying on fees such as card subscriptions.
With just £2.2 billion in loans at end-2025, Revolut's loan-to-deposit ratio of 6% compares with 55% for HSBC and 86% for Societe Generale.
Scaling its lending business will introduce risks including managing big and complex credit exposures, while entering fiercely competitive local mortgage markets will not be easy, analysts and investors said.
TOO FEW PRIMARY ACCOUNTS Revolut has attracted customers with its easy-to-use app but executives acknowledge too few use it as a primary bank account.
Revolut declined to comment in its latest results on how many customers did so in 2025, but said the figure was up 45% from a year ago.
This metric is a focus for Revolut's biggest backers.
Alex Immerman, an investor at Andreessen Horowitz, which is known as "a16z", told Reuters it was watching for primary-account adoption, as well as total customer balances.
($1 = 0.7573 pounds)

items.title: Leftist, nationalists set to win election for Bosnia's tripartite presidency
items.author: Branko Filipovic, Fedja Grulovic
items.creator: Branko Filipovic, Fedja Grulovic
items.summary: Voters are casting ballots for the central tripartite presidency and national parliament.
items.body:
A Bosniak left-leaning moderate, a pro-Russian Serb nationalist and a Croatian nationalist are leading Sunday's election for Bosnia's inter-ethnic tripartite presidency, the election commission said early on Monday, based on ballots from 96.31% of polling stations.
The results were largely in line with expectations and with projections by the Poliwave tracking platform, although voter turnout was low at a combined 42.02% in Bosnia's two entities, the Bosniak-Croat Federation and the Serb Republika Srpska. Voters also cast ballots for the national parliament, alongside regional races in the two entities.
Voter frustration has grown over an economic slowdown, the slow pace of EU entry talks and a lingering political crisis in which ethnically based dominant parties from the two entities have repeatedly stalled decisions by the weak central government that links them.
Denis Becirovic, a Bosniak of the Social Democratic Party (SDP-BiH) and part of the current tripartite presidency, garnered 26.78% of votes in the Bosniak-Croat Federation, ahead of the candidate for the centre-right Muslim Party of Democratic Action (SDA). The two had been considered favourites in the election.
Also leading in the Bosniak-Croat Federation was newcomer Darijana Filipovic of the nationalist and pro-European Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ-BiH), with 13.89% of the vote.
In Republika Srpska, Zeljka Cvijanovic, an existing member of the tripartite presidency from the Serb and pro-Russian nationalist Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD), secured 55.41% of votes, the election commission said.
Voting continued in some polling stations after the 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) deadline on Sunday due to delays related to a new electronic balloting system, Bosnia's Central Election Commission head Jovan Kalaba told reporters in Sarajevo.
The election commission redesigned ballots and introduced new biometric voter identification and electronic scanners, which it said were aimed at curbing voting fraud.
Speaking in Banja Luka, the largest Bosnian Serb city, Milorad Dodik, a separatist and pro-Russian leader of the SNSD who visited Moscow and met Russian President Vladimir Putin last week, said his party's candidate Savo Minic won the most votes for president of the Republika Srpska entity.
"We have won the member of the (Bosnian) Presidency, and the president of the Republika Srpska. An unexpectedly high result," Dodik said.
Since the Bosnian war ended in 1995 under the US-brokered Dayton peace accord, the country has been split along ethnic lines into two entities linked by the weak central government and tripartite presidency.
Bosnia, which has struggled to recover from the 1992-95 war, secured EU candidate status in December 2022 and approval to open accession negotiations in 2024. Actual talks have not started, however, because the domestic legislatures have yet to enact core requirements such as bolstering judicial oversight and passing anti-corruption laws.
Borjana Kristo, the deputy head of the Croat HDZ-BiH, said that overall progress could be made through dialogue after the elections.
"Bosnia must make progress solely on the principle of consensus, dialogue, and mutual respect," she told party supporters, cautioning against rhetoric that would drag the country backwards.
Many voters in the country of 3.4 million people say they want to move beyond divisive rhetoric but its politics have become deadlocked.
The EU and Russia have been vying for influence over Bosnia, with the EU seeking to expand its membership across the Balkans while Russia wants to slow that process down and preserve its influence over the Republika Srpska.
The US has also sought to bolster its influence in Bosnia, pushing for a $1.5 billion [USN:L6N40Y0SF TEXT:"pipeline project"] to import US liquefied natural gas. The EU has said, however, that the selection of the company for the project lacked competitive transparency, while Washington and Brussels have also clashed over the role of the [USN:L6N41N07W TEXT:"High Representative"], the international peace overseer for the country.

Oct 3 : The White House has created a task force to examine AI's risks and opportunities and recommend what role the federal government should play in overseeing the technology, with a report due within 120 days, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing the head of the task force, Jay Clayton.
Clayton, who heads the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, said he would lead the group, known as the "Super Intelligence Force," effectively serving as US President Donald Trump's AI czar, the report said, citing a senior White House official.

Oct 3 : A former OpenAI safety employee who recently resigned criticized the company's approach to AI safety, arguing that a fast-paced culture focused on rapid development increases the risk of failures.
Writing in "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken," published by the Atlantic on Saturday, David Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being "nearly careful enough" and should place greater emphasis on safety expertise and research before developing more capable systems.
• "The time for trial and error is over," Robinson wrote, arguing that advanced AI systems require safeguards more akin to those used in industries such as nuclear power and aviation.
• Robinson said OpenAI relies heavily on what it calls "iterative deployment," releasing systems and strengthening safeguards when problems emerge.

• The comments add to a debate within the AI industry over whether companies are moving too quickly to develop increasingly powerful systems. OpenAI and rival Anthropic have faced scrutiny after incidents in which safety controls failed, or experimental systems behaved unexpectedly.
• Robinson, who said he spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches, wrote: "As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed."
• "We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement.
• Robinson also warned that AI capabilities were advancing faster than researchers' understanding of alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems act in accordance with human goals and values.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Ukraine will hit Russian refineries in response to Moscow's 'new doctrine' of airstrikes, Zelenskiy says
items.author: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
items.creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
items.summary: Vladimir Putin called for broader attacks on civilian targets, Volodymyr Zelenskiy told Reuters.
items.body:
Ukraine will double down on attacking Russian oil refineries in response to a new policy of airstrikes by Moscow designed to [USN:L8N44V1KC TEXT:"force people to abandon Kyiv"] and other cities, but will not target civilians, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.
Ukraine's intelligence services has obtained documents showing that Russian leader Vladimir Putin had issued a "new doctrine" of military attacks on a much broader range of civilian targets ahead of this winter, Zelenskiy said.
"We saw documents and we know that they allow them to attack infrastructure, logistics, and especially to attack in the cities, in the villages, everywhere, roads, schools, hospitals," Zelenskiy told Reuters in an interview. "To pressure people to leave the capital, leave different cities: this is the goal of the operation."
Driving the shift in policy, Zelenskiy said, was Putin's desire to appear strong at a time when his military was losing ground in a key frontline region and sustaining higher levels of casualties.
The Kremlin was not available to comment on Saturday. But in a statement [USN:L1N45P03K TEXT:"urging foreign nationals to leave Kyiv"], the Russian Foreign Ministry said Moscow would continue to systematically hit targets in what it said were retaliatory strikes for Ukrainian attacks on Russia in recent months.
Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians.
COUNTEROFFENSIVE IN DONBAS Zelenskiy said a successful Ukrainian counteroffensive, code-named "Vivaldi", had recaptured around 140 sq km (54 sq miles) of Ukrain's eastern Donbas region and was still ongoing. Russia has said it must control Donbas in its entirety as a condition for any peace deal.
In recent weeks, US President Donald Trump's administration has sought to revive talks to end the four-year-old conflict – Europe's bloodiest since World War Two.
The US leader last month urged Ukraine [USN:L1N45503J TEXT:"to refrain from hitting Russian oil installations"], saying that was sending global diesel prices surging.
But Zelenskiy, speaking as air raid sirens blared outside the gilded halls of the presidential offices, said he had received no indications from Russia that Putin was interested in peace talks, or discussing a ceasefire on energy infrastructure.
Over the past week, the Ukrainian capital has come under persistent attack by Russian drones and missiles targeting energy and telecoms assets, road and rail infrastructure. For the first time, Russia has [USN:L1N45P00Z TEXT:"targeted the bridges"] across the Dnipro river connecting east and west Kyiv.
Zelenskiy said Ukraine would react to the change in tactics by Moscow, but would not target civilian infrastructure indiscriminately.
"We have to respond in any way (we can). With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners etc: what gives money to them for this war," Zelenskiy said in English. "But we will not respond, of course, just like them, on any civilian objects."
SUPPORT FROM EUROPE After the Trump administration invited Putin [USN:L6N45F16H TEXT:"to attend a G20 summit in Miami"] in December and discussed business deals with Russian envoys, Zelenskiy urged Washington not to normalise relations with Russia before ensuring a return to peace.
Zelenskiy said he would be happy to meet Putin for peace talks at the G20, but he warned the US not to believe in "illusions" that Russia would simply end hostilities if it gained control of Donbas.
"It's not fair just to normalise," said Zelenskiy, dressed in his trademark black T-shirt and military-style jacket. Any resumption of economic and diplomatic ties with the West had to be in return for Russia ending hostilities, he said: "Because peace is more important than any kind of economy."
While the US has proposed a resumption of trilateral talks in the coming weeks in the UAE, Zelenskiy noted that an exact date and location for the technical-level conversations had still not been set.
Ukrainian officials warn that Russia has stockpiled hundreds of ballistic missiles ahead of an expected winter onslaught against electricity and water infrastructure. Last winter, the worst of the war, Russian strikes left swathes of the country without electricity and heating for days at a time.
Since the summer, Moscow has also begun launching dozens of fast and relatively cheap jet-powered Shahed drones a day at Ukraine, whose air defence teams have struggled to cope because their interceptor drones were too slow to catch them.
Zelenskiy said Ukraine had been forced to rely heavily on its fighter aircraft – F-16s and MiGs – to down around 60% of the Russian jet-powered drones, but supplies of 20 mm ammunition for the planes were running low.
Kyiv was urgently working on other solutions – including boosting its electronic jamming capabilities, he said. In the second half of October, it would receive the first shipment of small, cheap air defence missiles capable of hitting the new Shaheds.
Last week, Zelenskiy said Ukraine was developing five models of new interceptor drones capable of downing the jet Shaheds. Fresh from a meeting with his defence chiefs, he said tests on two of those models showed a modest success rate of around 30%.
"We'll have to scale it," he said. "I hope that with all these things, with all these elements, we'll find a way."
BALLISTIC THREAT Ukraine announced the first combat use this week of its own domestically made ballistic missile, the FP-7, which has a range of around 250 km (155 miles).
Zelenskiy said he had called the manufacturer Fire Point to pressure executives to finish a longer-range model, the FP-9, which the company has said could hit Moscow.
"I said to them, where is my FP-9?" said Zelenskiy, with a grin. "We need the FP-9. And the FP-9 will be (ready) this autumn, I'm sure."
Zelenskiy said a recent spate of Russian drone incursions and hybrid attacks in Europe were an effort to intimidate European populations and to undermine support for Ukraine.
Some European leaders were starting to understand this, he said, and toughen their position.
Russia says such accusations are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria.
After talks with European officials in Brussels this week, Ukraine had unlocked funding to order the drones that it needs to keep fighting at the start of 2027, Zelenskiy said.
Ukrainian officials had worked on plans with European partners to plug a $27 billion hole in Kyiv's defence budget this year.
The plans involve a combination of the reallocation of Ukraine's own budget resources, bilateral assistance and using "money credits" from next year's portion of a €90 billion EU loan, Zelenskiy said.
"We will close this (gap). I think this is absolutely a big success for our country," he said.

LONDON: Two Iranian nationals appeared in a London court on Saturday (Oct 3) charged with plotting acts of terrorism involving the use of a homemade bomb to attack the Jewish community in northern England at the behest of a figure believed to be based in Iran.
Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were arrested on Sep 20 at the start of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, when they are accused of carrying out "hostile" surveillance on potential Jewish targets in Manchester, prosecutors say.
These targets included the Manchester Jewish Museum and Heaton Park synagogue, the scene of a deadly attack almost a year ago in which two Jewish worshippers were killed, prosecutor Mark Luckett told Westminster Magistrates' Court.
ALLEGED PLOT INVOLVED HOMEMADE DEVICE "Both defendants are accused of preparing acts of terrorism targeting the Jewish community in Manchester through the use of a homemade explosive device," Luckett said.

He said the men were accused of being in contact with a third party who is alleged to have directed and coordinated the attack planning and provided instructions on how to assemble a homemade device, which prosecutors allege would have been made from chlorine and brake fluid.
"It's assessed that this individual is also an Iranian national and most likely operating from within Iran," Luckett said.

Related:

UK's Starmer convenes community leaders to fight antisemitism after attacks

Two Jewish men stabbed in London, police treat attack as terrorism

The court was told both men had come to Britain from Europe in small boats. Salehi had arrived in 2020 and had been granted asylum, while Ahmadyan came in 2023 and his asylum claim was still outstanding, Luckett said.
The men did not enter a plea and were remanded in custody until their next hearing at London's Old Bailey court on Oct 23.
The case comes a week after Britain said Iran was believed to be involved in a suspected plot to target the RAF Fairford air base which the US military has used to carry out raids against targets in Iran, leading to a dual British-Iranian national being arrested on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts.
Police said on Saturday he had been released on police bail while the investigation continues. British counterterrorism police have said the Manchester allegations were not connected in any way to the Fairford investigation.
Iran has rejected accusations of involvement in a number of plots in Britain in recent years, and said allegations it was connected to the Fairford incident were baseless.
Britain has also seen a significant rise in antisemitism since the Hamas attacks on Israel in October 2023 that triggered the subsequent war in Gaza, including a series of attacks on Jewish sites in London earlier this year.
"It is no secret that this country faces a range of serious threats from the Iranian regime," Home Secretary (interior minister) Shabana Mahmood said in a statement.
"They target our Jewish communities and try to silence their critics overseas, often through proxies and criminal networks to hide their involvement."

Source: Reuters/ec

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 3 : US President Donald Trump spent Tuesday showcasing his administration’s approach to AI — touting the US government’s new AI chatbot, dining with tech titans at the White House, and announcing a voluntary agreement with those executives that he said would address growing fears about the technology's safety.
The display signaled that Trump is eager to show he is addressing growing voter concerns about AI's dangers without imposing restrictions that could hamper the technology's development, AI safety advocates said. The safety agreement with six companies — Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Alphabet’s Google — includes no stated consequences if a company chooses not to comply. Trump described it as “morally binding.”
“This was an attempt to give the impression that the government is listening to these concerns without undercutting what has been a very clear and consistent line from this administration: that regulation and governance inherently impede innovation,” said Kat Duffy, who runs an AI team at the nonpartisan Council on Foreign Relations.
Whether voters buy Trump's effort in the run-up to US midterm elections on November 3 remains to be seen. Public uneasiness with AI, and the small group of people who seemingly hold sway over it, has risen in recent months. Three-quarters of Americans worry that AI companies have not gone far enough to prevent AI from causing serious harm to society, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll published September 22. A series of security events has also underscored how advanced AI can act unpredictably.

Hundreds of OpenAI AI agents broke out of their testing environment in July and attacked the infrastructure of AI platform Hugging Face. In early September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, saying that the people building AI believe it "could kill us all by the end of the decade." His words, and others, sparked a flurry of calls from US lawmakers for AI regulation. 
Through it all, Trump has largely dismissed those concerns, saying that government restrictions would make it harder for American companies to compete against their Chinese counterparts. He has repeatedly said that US law enforcement agencies such as the Justice Department serve as sufficient guardrails, and that no new rules are needed. He also directed his administration to call AI "super intelligence," part of an effort to improve the reputation of an unpopular technology. 
The concerns have become prominent enough to make their way into late-night comedy. In late September, "Saturday Night Live" satirized Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, one of the industry's most outspoken voices on AI risks — even as his company readies a public stock sale that could value it at $2 trillion — with cast member Jane Wickline portraying the executive.
"AI is not a weapon, it’s a tool: A tool for building weapons. And I urge you to urge me to stop," Wickline said as Amodei.
CONCERNS ABOUT ENFORCEMENT
The accord, inked Tuesday, does include measures that AI safety advocates have sought, including calling for “robust internal controls” to prevent unauthorized hacks as well as partnering with “independent external auditors.” Those concepts have been included in draft state and federal legislation, and California in September enacted the first state law setting rules for how independent auditors evaluate AI products.
But the one-page White House document did not address details or enforcement mechanisms.
A White House official said in a statement that the agreement will "advance American innovation and strengthen responsible development" of AI models. Trump is expected to name his Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as his top AI adviser, Reuters previously reported, a position he has dubbed "AI czar," even as Clayton stays in his role leading the nation's intelligence agencies.
Representative Ro Khanna, a Democrat representing Silicon Valley, welcomed the idea of "independent auditors" but said that they should report to an independent federal agency.
"They can’t just be auditors that report to (OpenAI CEO) Sam Altman or Dario Amodei," he said. "My concern is the president basically trusting these guys who have a huge profit motive and won’t have the judgment to keep us safe."
Venture capitalist David Sacks, who advises Trump on AI and has been an advocate for unrestricted AI development, said on the social media platform X that securities law and other legal authorities would penalize companies that fail to address problems uncovered by internal controls or auditors.
But AI safety advocates told Reuters those authorities can only address harms after they occur, saying the threats require safeguards designed to prevent large-scale harm before it happens.
Nevertheless, some AI observers saw the simple fact of hosting the event as an indication that Trump is absorbing the worries.
Trump’s agreement with the tech executives is “a shift toward acknowledging that there are serious safety and security concerns that merit closer coordination between the companies,” said Samuel Hammond, AI policy director at the conservative Foundation for American Innovation.

Source: Reuters

MANILA: The Philippines, chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), expressed concern over an airstrike in Myanmar's Rakhine state that caused deaths, injuries and destruction, and stood ready to facilitate discussions within the regional bloc on how best to assist Myanmar.
"The Philippines is closely monitoring developments and expresses concern over the attacks which resulted in destruction, loss of lives and injuries to those affected," Foreign Affairs Assistant Secretary for ASEAN Affairs Ana Marie Hernando said in an email response on Saturday (Oct 3).
As ASEAN chair, Manila said it remained mindful of the views of all member states and would continue to be guided by the regional bloc's consensus-based approach.
The Philippines said it stood ready to facilitate discussions within ASEAN on ways to assist Myanmar, in line with the common aspiration of finding a solution that is "Myanmar-owned and led".
Monday's Kyauktaw airstrike, Rakhine's deadliest such attack since a December hospital bombing, killed 50 people and wounded dozens more.
Myanmar has been locked in a nationwide civil war since a 2021 coup, with an alliance of armed groups, including the Arakan Army, fighting against the military.
The protracted conflict has since killed around 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million in the impoverished Southeast Asian nation.

Source: Reuters/js

AUBERVILLIERS: Maisa, a 17-year-old in a poor Paris suburb who aspires to be an English teacher, joined tens of thousands of other students and their supporters this week in protests that spread across France over dilapidated schools, classroom overcrowding and teacher shortages. 
At Lycee Le Corbusier school in Aubervilliers, a suburb north of Paris in the Seine-Saint-Denis department, protesters said schools in poor neighbourhoods like theirs faced the worst conditions.
“Last year I took the high school French exam without a French teacher, and teachers have a huge impact,” Maisa said.
"These are not conditions to study in."

As protests raged at more than 1,200 French high schools this week, police responded with tear gas and rubber bullets in some cases. More than 5,000 people were arrested, and some protesters were seriously hurt with eye injuries, broken teeth and blows to the head. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez called it a "climate of unacceptable violence" and called for order.
Amelia, 15, joined Maisa in the crowd outside the school gates and held a sign reading, "Our address should not decide our future". She said she was demonstrating to demand the same rights as students elsewhere in the country.      
"The education authority is not investing enough in the suburbs. It's classist and racist," she said. 
Ulysse Rabate, a political scientist at Paris 8 University, said the protests show the way that France's marginalised urban neighbourhoods are increasingly influencing national politics.
"When there is a collapse of the public service, of public education, those who feel it the most, and the most violently, are those at bottom," he said.

A French firefighter extinguishes a fire on the street amid clashes between protesters and police during a high school students protest in Pantin near Paris as part of nationwide protests to demand the hiring of substitute teachers, increased resources and better learning conditions, as more than 400 schools remain closed following days of student protests that have escalated into violence in some places, France, Oct 2, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Tom Nicholson)

POLITICAL FLASHPOINT The nationwide demonstrations and blockades , which began last week, have become a political flashpoint at a sensitive moment for the government, which announced a series of deeply unpopular spending cuts in its 2027 budget on Thursday.
The education budget is set to increase by a below-inflation 1.7 per cent to €65.53 billion, excluding teacher pensions.
The education ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Education Minister Edouard Geffray said that education remained a priority and the below-inflation budget increase was due to population decline.
The protests started in the Parisian suburbs, where poverty levels are high, then spread to Paris itself and other French towns, including Marseille, Strasbourg, Tours and Lille. 
At Lycee Le Corbusier, classes including maths, humanities, English and sport have been canceled since the start of the academic year due to a teacher shortage, according to Karima Kara Ali, an elected parent representative. 
In Seine-Saint-Denis, two-thirds of high schools took part in protests on Thursday, the CGT labour union said. Youth, teachers and parents in four towns complained of unsanitary school conditions and chronic staff shortages including of nurses and social workers. 
Louise Paternoster, a representative for the Seine-Saint-Denis branch of the CGT's education union, said the area does not get adequate resources for its student population and their educational needs.
Two-thirds of schools in the department have unfilled teacher positions, according to a union survey.

A student carries a barrier in front of a banner which reads "equal opportunities" suspended on the front of Louis-le-Grand high school in central Paris, on Oct 2, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Simon Wohlfahrt)

NOT ENOUGH TEACHERS "Our students are losing out on study time. Some schools don't have drinking water. We are not equal to other departments," she said, blaming shortages on government cuts of 3,256 teacher positions nationwide in 2026.
In Pantin, a town on the northeastern edge of Paris, teacher Dilan Roche joined her students as they protested outside their school this week to support their demands and protect them from the police.
"What they wrote on banners, we wrote in a letter to the local education authority: overcrowded classes, no nurses, no social workers - which is problematic for students with learning difficulties, many living in precarity," she said.
While France ranks in the middle of OECD countries for spending on education, the average expenditure per secondary school student has remained little changed over the last decade, standing at €11,660 in 2024 and €11,910 in 2010, according to education ministry data. 
The last nationwide high school protest movement on this scale demanding more funding came in the 1990s. That followed the government sharply expanding access to the baccalauréat, the school-leaving exam that typically paves the way to university, without providing schools with sufficient additional resources, said Professor Clemence Cardon-Quint at Paul Valery University, who researches education funding. 
The movement won an increase in funding, but spending per student later stagnated despite growing demands on schools.
Cardon-Quint said students and teachers have taken on additional responsibilities over the years, including navigating Parcoursup, the university admissions system introduced in 2018 and criticised by some students and teachers as opaque and discriminatory.
"In a period of budgetary restraint, it is more difficult to reduce inequalities," said Cardon-Quint.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［フランクフルト　２日　ロイター］ - ドイツ連邦銀行（中央銀行）のナーゲル総裁は２日、同国の今年の成長率が１％前後...
items.body:
独経済、今年1％前後成長も　財政支出と輸出寄与と連銀総裁
10/3 15:46 配信

2023年11月、キプロス中央銀行で開催された会合で撮影　REUTERS/Yiannis Kourtoglou

［フランクフルト　２日　ロイター］ - ドイツ連邦銀行（中央銀行）のナーゲル総裁は２日、同国の今年の成長率が１％前後になる可能性があると述べた。堅調な輸出需要と政府投資が寄与する。同中銀が６月に示した予測（０．５％）の２倍となる。

ドイツは過去３年間ほとんど成長していない。イラン戦争に起因するエネルギー価格高騰が産業に打撃を与えている。

ナーゲル氏は講演で、生産は予想外に底堅いと指摘した。潜在成長率は依然として低いものの、ドイツは景気循環上の回復局面にあるとの認識を示した。

「年平均で１％前後の実質経済成長となる可能性は十分にある」と述べ、「３年間の停滞を経て、これは確かに小さいながらも歓迎すべき兆しとなるだろう」とした。

ナーゲル氏は、連邦政府の国防やインフラなどに重点を置いた財政支出を成長けん引役の一つとし、予想外に堅調な海外需要の恩恵も受けているとした。

ドイツの主要経済研究所も先月下旬に、今年と来年の経済成長率予測を上方修正した。今年の成長率予測は０．６％から１．３％に引き上げられた。

items.author: ロイター

items.summary:
Stephen Nellis

[サンフランシスコ ２日 ロイター] - 米アップルは２日、同社のＰＣ「Ｍａｃ」の基本ソ...
items.body:
アップル、Ｍａｃのアクセス権限制御強化へ　ＡＩリスク対策
10/3 13:57 配信

3月にニューヨーク市で開催されたアップルのイベント　REUTERS/Shannon Stapleton

Stephen Nellis

[サンフランシスコ ２日 ロイター] - 米アップルは２日、同社のＰＣ「Ｍａｃ」の基本ソフト（ＯＳ）を修正すると明らかにした。人工知能（ＡＩ）エージェントがＭａｃ内の全データへのアクセスを求めた場合に、利用者がより明確に認識し対応できるようにする。

メタ・プラットフォームズのＡＩエージェント「Ｍｕｓｅ」について、一部ユーザーから、機密性の高い個人情報にアクセスされたとの批判が出ている。

アップルのスマートフォン「ｉＰｈｏｎｅ」やタブレット端末「ｉＰａｄ」では、「サンドボックス化」と呼ばれる仕組みにより、初期設定ではどのアプリも別のアプリ内のデータにアクセスできない。一方、Ｍａｃはより柔軟な設計となっており、利用者の許可があれば、クラウドバックアップサービスなどのアプリが端末内の全データにアクセスできる「フルディスクアクセス」という設定がある。

アップルは２日、自社のサイトで、一部の開発者が利用者を危険にさらしかねない形でフルディスクアクセス機能を使っていると指摘し、今後、追加の制御機能を導入すると表明した。

「ＡＩエージェントの能力と自律性が高まるにつれ、これほど広範なアクセスに伴うリスクは大幅に増大する。利用者が自身のデータとプライバシーについて十分な情報に基づいて判断できるよう、アクセスを許可する前にこうしたリスクを明確に理解できるようにすることに取り組む」とした。

[２日 ロイター] - 米クリーブランド地区連銀のハマック総裁は２日、９月の米雇用...
items.body:
9月雇用統計はトレンドに整合、次回会合までにさらなる情報＝クリーブランド連銀総裁
10/3 10:19 配信

ニューヨーク市で2025年11月撮影　REUTERS/Brendan McDermid/File Photo

Michael S. Derby

[２日 ロイター] - 米クリーブランド地区連銀のハマック総裁は２日、９月の米雇用統計は最近の雇用情勢と整合的との認識を示した上で、今後の金融政策を決めるまでにはまだ時間があると述べた。

ハマック氏は米公共放送ＰＢＳの番組「ニュースアワー」のインタビューで、「過去１２カ月は平均で毎月４万１０００人の雇用が生まれている。これは私が推計する（雇用セクターの）ブレークイーブンとおおむね一致する」と述べ、労働市場が安定的に推移していることを示唆するとした。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の金融政策対応については、「月末の会合までに、さらに多くの情報が得られる。２つの責務を確実に果たせるよう、適切な政策スタンスを決める時間は十分にある」と語った。

ＦＲＢは先月、約３年ぶりに０．２５％ポイントの利上げを決定した。ハマック氏は、早い段階から利上げを支持してきた。

今週、複数のＦＲＢ高官が、追加利上げの前にデータを見極める時間があるとの認識を示した。また９月の雇用統計発表後、１０月２７─２８日の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での利上げ観測が後退し、ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチでは据え置きの確率が８６％となっている。

items.summary:

[ヒューストン　２日　ロイター] - 米国時間の原油先物は反落して取引を終えた。欧州首脳が、価...
items.body:
原油先物反落、Ｇ７が石油備蓄1億バレル協調放出で合意
10/3 6:28 配信

英ロンドンのガソリンスタンドで２日撮影。REUTERS/Toby Melville

Erwin Seba

[ヒューストン　２日　ロイター] - 米国時間の原油先物は反落して取引を終えた。欧州首脳が、価格引き下げに向けてディーゼル燃料（軽油）の備蓄を放出するよう求めていた米国の要請に応じることで合意した。

清算値は、北海ブレント先物が０．０６ドル（０．０６％）安の１バレル＝１０２．２５ドル。米ＷＴＩ先物は１．７６ドル（１．９０％）安の１バレル＝９１．１１ドル。

主要７カ国（Ｇ７）は２日の首脳共同声明で、世界のエネルギー市場の安定化に向け、国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）を通じてディーゼル燃料などの石油備蓄１億バレルを協調放出すると発表した。Ｇ７の発表に先立ち、トランプ米大統領は交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」への投稿で「欧州は大量に備蓄しているディーゼルを大規模に放出することに合意した。手続きは直ちに開始される」と表明していた。

プライス・フューチャーズ・グループのシニアアナリスト、フィル・フリン氏は「欧州はかなり脆弱だと感じている」とし、「（米国が）ディーゼルの輸出禁止を発動すれば、欧州は最も打撃を受ける地域の１つとなるだろう」と述べた。

items.title: 米国株式市場＝続伸、雇用統計受け利上げ観測後退　小型株高い
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Chuck Mikolajczak

[ニューヨーク　２日　ロイター] - 米国株式市場は続伸して取引を終えた。この日発...
items.body:
米国株式市場＝続伸、雇用統計受け利上げ観測後退　小型株高い
10/3 6:26 配信

ニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）前で２０２１年７月撮影。REUTERS/Andrew Kelly

Chuck Mikolajczak

[ニューヨーク　２日　ロイター] - 米国株式市場は続伸して取引を終えた。この日発表された雇用統計の内容を受け、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）による今月の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での利上げ観測が後退した。

米労働省労働統計局が発表した９月の雇用統計によると、非農業部門雇用者数は２万９０００人増で、前月から伸びが鈍化し市場予想を下回った。過去２カ月分も大幅に下方改定された。失業率は４．２％で、前月の４．１％から上昇した。

これを受け、ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、ＦＲＢが１０月のＦＯＭＣで少なくとも２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）利上げするとの観測は２２．７％と、前日の２４．４％、１週間前の６４．２％から低下した。 

ニューヨークのサミットＴＸキャピタルのトレーディング責任者ロバート・バーンストン氏は「本日の統計は、景気が急速に過熱していないという意味では悪くない」と指摘。その上で、「しかし、短期的な利上げ観測を後退させる点では良いが、景気やインフレを巡る懸念もあるため、市場は慎重ながらも楽観的な姿勢を取っている」と述べた。

利上げ観測の後退を受け、金利に敏感な銘柄が買われた。Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種の不動産セクターは０．４％高、中小型株で構成するラッセル２０００指数は０．９％高と、１日としては過去１カ月で最大の上昇率となった。

大型株も相場をけん引し、エヌビディアは１．３％高、 テスラは４．７％高と、Ｓ＆Ｐ５００種を大きく押し上げた。テスラの上昇を受けＳ＆Ｐの一般消費財セクターは１．４％ 高と、Ｓ＆Ｐ５００の主要１１業種のうち最も高いパフォーマンスとなった。

スポーツ用品大手ナイキは３．６％安。同社は１日、２０２７会計年度売上高が１桁台後半の減少率になるとの見通しを示したほか、追加の人員削減や世界事業の再編を含む新たな経営改善策を発表した。

データ記憶装置メーカーの株価も下落。ウエスタン・デジタルとシーゲイト・テクノロジーはいずれも約１０％急落し、Ｓ＆Ｐの情報技術セクターで下落率トップとなった。東芝が２０２７年度中に人工知能（ＡＩ）データセンター向けのハードディスクドライブ（ＨＤＤ）の生産能力を倍増すると日経新聞が報じたことが材料となった。

ニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）では値上がり銘柄数が値下がり銘柄数を１．６７対１の比率で上回ったほか、ナスダックでも１．３４対１で値上がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は１６９億３０００万株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７２億８０００万株。

items.body:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル、対ユーロで4週連続高へ　雇用統計受け上昇一服
10/3 6:16 配信

2025年5月4日撮影。 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

［ニューヨーク　２日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが対ユーロで４週連続で上昇する見通し。ユーロ圏債の売りを背景に米債利回りが上昇しているほか、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が引き続きタカ派的な金融政策スタンスを維持するとの期待がドルを支援している。

ただ、２日発表された米雇用統計を受け、ドルは最近の上昇分を一部削った。９月の雇用統計では、非農業部門雇用者数が２万９０００人増で、前月から伸びが鈍化し市場予想を下回った。失業率は４．２％で、前月の４．１％から上昇した。

ノムラのＧ１０為替戦略責任者ドミニク・バニング氏は、雇用統計が全体として「ゴルディロックス（適温）」状態を示唆したと指摘。「経済活動は引き続きかなり堅調だが、大きなインフレ圧力を生み出していない」と述べた。その上で、市場が織り込む米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の利上げ見通しを大きく変える可能性は低いとしつつも、「１０月の追加利上げを巡るテールリスクを幾分後退させる効果はあるだろう」と述べた。

ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、市場はＦＲＢが８６％の確率で１０月に金利を据え置くと見込んでいる。１週間前は３６％だった。

終盤の取引で、ユーロ／ドルは０．１３％高の１．１２５８０ドル。ただ、ユーロは週間では４週連続での下げとなる見通しで、これは２０２５年５月半ば以来最長となる。

主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．１％安の１０１．８８。ただ、週足では３週連続で上昇する見込み。

ドル／円は０．１５％安の１５７．８１円。ただ、ドルは週間で３週連続の上昇となる見通し。

ドル／スイスフランも０．３％安の０．８２８５フラン。

また、ユーロ圏金融・債券市場では、財政問題の悪化とインフレ高進を巡る懸念から、仏１０年債利回りが約２５年ぶりに５％近辺まで上昇する場面があった。

ユーロは対スイスフランで０．１５％安の０．９３２７フラン、対円では横ばいの１７７．６７円となった。週間ベースでは、ユーロはスイスフラン、円双方に対し下落する見通し。
